title: Net electricity from an integrated fusion plant
subfield: Energy gain, ignition, and burning plasmas
open: Demonstrate positive net electricity exported over a complete operating cycle, including drivers, magnets, cryogenics, pumps, fuel processing, startup, and recovery.
status: Target gain above unity is established in inertial confinement; it is not plant-level electrical gain. The 2026 DOE roadmap still treats integrated fusion electricity as a development objective.
why: This separates a fusion experiment from an electricity-generating technology.
key_works: NASEM (2021), *Bringing Fusion to the U.S. Grid*, DOI: 10.17226/25991; DOE (2026), *Fusion Science and Technology Roadmap*.

title: Sustained alpha-dominated magnetic-confinement operation
subfield: Energy gain, ignition, and burning plasmas
open: Sustain a magnetically confined plasma in which fusion alpha particles supply most heating while density, impurities, pressure, and current remain controlled.
status: Decades of externally heated experiments support extrapolation, but the cited gain surveys distinguish these from sustained reactor-like burning operation.
why: External heating can conceal instabilities and power-balance problems that appear when the plasma heats itself.
key_works: Wurzel and Hsu (2022), *Progress toward fusion energy breakeven and gain as measured against the Lawson criterion*, DOI: 10.1063/5.0083990; arXiv:2105.10954.

title: Robust burn-control stability
subfield: Energy gain, ignition, and burning plasmas
open: Establish and experimentally validate a controller that stabilizes fusion power against coupled temperature, density, ash, and confinement perturbations without excessive auxiliary power.
status: Burning-plasma dynamics are modeled, but reactor-scale closed-loop validation remains part of the ITER research program.
why: A favorable equilibrium is insufficient if disturbances repeatedly terminate the burn.
key_works: Loarte et al. (2025), *Required R&D in existing fusion facilities to support the new baseline ITER Research Plan*, ITR-25-005.

title: Helium-ash removal without fuel loss
subfield: Energy gain, ignition, and burning plasmas
open: Demonstrate selective removal of thermalized helium ash while retaining sufficient deuterium and tritium and preserving core confinement.
status: Particle-transport and exhaust studies exist; self-consistent ash removal in a sustained, strongly self-heated reactor plasma remains unvalidated.
why: Accumulated helium dilutes fuel and can extinguish an otherwise viable burn.
key_works: Greenfield, Collins, and workshop contributors (2023), *Report of the US ITER Research Program Research Needs Workshop*, arXiv:2303.12094.

title: Alpha-particle redistribution under overlapping modes
subfield: Energy gain, ignition, and burning plasmas
open: Predict alpha redistribution and wall losses when several energetic-particle modes overlap, including nonlinear saturation and evolving background profiles.
status: Single-mode theory and extensive experiments exist; the burning-plasma, multimode extrapolation remains a central uncertainty.
why: Alpha losses simultaneously reduce heating and concentrate damaging power on walls.
key_works: Chen and Zonca (2016), *Physics of Alfvén waves and energetic particles in burning plasmas*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.88.015008.

title: Predictive energetic-particle mode saturation
subfield: Energy gain, ignition, and burning plasmas
open: Determine when energetic-particle instabilities saturate harmlessly, chirp, avalanche, or produce large transport bursts, using a model validated across devices.
status: Nonlinear theories explain important regimes, but no universal reactor-validated saturation rule follows from the existing review literature.
why: Linear instability thresholds alone cannot establish acceptable alpha confinement.
key_works: Chen and Zonca (2016), *Physics of Alfvén waves and energetic particles in burning plasmas*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.88.015008.

title: Useful alpha channeling
subfield: Energy gain, ignition, and burning plasmas
open: Transfer a substantial, measured fraction of fusion-alpha energy into useful fuel heating or current drive, with the full wave-generation power included.
status: Theory and proposed operating schemes exist; economically useful reactor-scale alpha channeling has not been established by the cited work.
why: It could reduce recirculating power and improve the prospects of difficult fuels.
key_works: Ochs et al. (2022), *Improving the Feasibility of Economical Proton-Boron 11 Fusion via Alpha Channeling with a Hybrid Fast and Thermal Proton Scheme*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevE.106.055215; arXiv:2210.08076.

title: Low-recirculating-power access to the burning state
subfield: Energy gain, ignition, and burning plasmas
open: Find experimentally accessible startup trajectories that reach a stable high-gain state without requiring auxiliary systems that make the complete plant uneconomic.
status: Lawson-condition studies quantify gain requirements, but satisfying a steady-state condition does not establish an affordable path to it.
why: Startup hardware and repeated failed starts can dominate plant power and availability.
key_works: Wurzel and Hsu (2025), *Continuing progress toward fusion energy breakeven and gain as measured against the Lawson criteria*, arXiv:2505.03834.

title: Reactor-geometry Dimits-shift prediction
open: Predict the nonlinear turbulence threshold above the linear instability threshold in realistic electromagnetic, multispecies, shaped plasmas.
status: Reduced-model explanations and three-dimensional studies exist; a quantitatively reliable reactor-geometry theory remains incomplete.
why: The difference between linear and nonlinear thresholds strongly affects predicted confinement.
key_works: Ivanov et al. (2020), *Zonally dominated dynamics and Dimits threshold in curvature-driven ITG turbulence*, DOI: 10.1017/S0022377820000938; arXiv:2004.04047.

title: Predictive ion–electron turbulence coupling
open: Quantify when electron-scale turbulence changes ion-scale transport, and vice versa, across reactor-relevant gradients, magnetic geometry, and beta.
status: Multiscale simulations demonstrated enhanced transport from cross-scale coupling by 2014–2016; economical predictive coverage remains limited.
why: Simulating either scale alone can give the wrong heat loss.
key_works: Howard et al. (2016), *Multi-scale gyrokinetic simulations: Comparison with experiment and implications for predicting turbulence and transport*, *Physics of Plasmas* 23, 056109.

title: Microtearing saturation and electron heat transport
open: Predict nonlinear microtearing transport, including magnetic-island overlap, collisions, electron kinetics, and interaction with other turbulence.
status: Electromagnetic gyrokinetic studies exist, but predictive extrapolation across collisionality and geometry remains a research problem.
why: Electron heat loss can determine whether high-pressure operating points are viable.
key_works: Garbet et al. (2010), *Gyrokinetic simulations of turbulent transport*, DOI: 10.1088/0029-5515/50/4/043002; MGK SciDAC publication program.

title: Kinetic-ballooning transport beyond onset
open: Derive and validate transport predictions after kinetic-ballooning modes become unstable, rather than using their threshold alone.
status: Threshold calculations are incorporated into pedestal models; saturated electromagnetic transport remains harder to predict.
why: A threshold-based design can fail if post-threshold transport is unexpectedly strong.
key_works: Snyder et al. (2011), *A first-principles predictive model of the pedestal height and width: development, testing and ITER optimization with the EPED model*, *Nuclear Fusion* 51, 103016.

title: Intrinsic rotation in low-torque reactors
open: Predict the sign, magnitude, and radial profile of toroidal rotation without strong external momentum injection.
status: Specific mechanisms, including non-Maxwellian equilibrium effects, have been demonstrated theoretically; a universal quantitative prediction remains unavailable.
why: Rotation affects stability and transport, but reactor neutral beams may provide little torque.
key_works: Barnes et al. (2013), *Intrinsic Rotation Driven by Non-Maxwellian Equilibria in Tokamak Plasmas*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.111.055005.

title: Momentum-pinch closure
open: Separate diffusive, convective, and residual-stress contributions to momentum transport well enough to predict rotation changes under reactor operating transitions.
status: Theoretical decompositions exist, but their practical identification and extrapolation remain entangled with intrinsic-rotation physics.
why: Incorrect momentum transport predictions undermine stability-control requirements.
key_works: Barnes et al. (2013), *Intrinsic Rotation Driven by Non-Maxwellian Equilibria in Tokamak Plasmas*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.111.055005.

title: Hydrogen-isotope confinement effect
open: Explain and predict how confinement changes between hydrogen, deuterium, tritium, and mixtures after controlling for heating, profiles, walls, and operating regime.
status: The effect has decades of experimental history; the 2023 review documents multiple mechanisms and unresolved mixture physics.
why: Deuterium experiments must reliably predict deuterium–tritium performance.
key_works: Ida (2023), *Isotope effect of transport and key physics in the isotope mixture plasmas*, DOI: 10.1007/s41614-023-00126-3.

title: Fuel-density peaking without impurity accumulation
open: Identify controllable regimes that increase central fuel density without producing unacceptable inward transport of high-charge impurities.
status: Neoclassical and turbulent impurity models exist, but their combined reactor operating window is not established.
why: Density peaking can increase fusion power, whereas impurity peaking can terminate the discharge.
key_works: Donnel et al. (2018), *Self-consistent gyrokinetic modeling of neoclassical and turbulent impurity transport*, DOI: 10.1088/1741-4326/aa6ebb.

title: Non-trace impurity transport
open: Predict impurity transport when impurities modify turbulence, collisions, radiation, and equilibrium rather than behaving as passive tracers.
status: Limits of passive-impurity approximations were explicitly examined in 2020; reactor mixtures require wider validation.
why: Trace-species calculations can fail precisely when contamination becomes operationally dangerous.
key_works: Lesur et al. (2020), *Validity limits of the passive treatment of impurities in gyrokinetic tokamak simulations*, DOI: 10.1088/1741-4326/ab6e48.

title: Turbulence spreading across stable regions
open: Quantify how turbulence generated in one radial region penetrates linearly stable regions and alters transport barriers.
status: Global simulations reveal nonlocal behavior; local flux-tube calculations do not by themselves resolve it.
why: Local stability can overstate the protection supplied by a transport barrier.
key_works: Dif-Pradalier et al. (2022), *Transport barrier onset and edge turbulence shortfall in fusion plasmas*, arXiv:2206.04193.

title: Heat avalanches and extreme transport events
open: Establish when intermittent transport avalanches materially change confinement or wall loading beyond predictions based on average fluxes.
status: Avalanche-like behavior appears in transport studies; a validated reactor-scale extreme-event model remains missing.
why: Rare events can dominate safety margins even when average confinement is acceptable.
key_works: Dif-Pradalier et al. (2022), *Transport barrier onset and edge turbulence shortfall in fusion plasmas*, arXiv:2206.04193.

title: Universal zonal-flow transition law
open: Determine which features of turbulence-to-zonal-flow transitions survive changes in geometry, drive, dissipation, kinetic physics, and system size.
status: Reduced systems exhibit sharp transitions, including the 2025 Hasegawa–Wakatani study; universality in realistic plasmas is unresolved.
why: A robust transition law could turn turbulence suppression into a predictable design variable.
key_works: Guillon and Gürcan (2025), *Phase transition from turbulence to zonal flows in the Hasegawa–Wakatani system*, DOI: 10.1063/5.0242282.

title: Reactor-scale transport similarity
open: Determine the corrections to gyro-Bohm and empirical confinement scaling as normalized gyroradius decreases toward reactor values.
status: Gyrokinetic theory supplies similarity arguments, but simultaneous reactor values of size, beta, collisionality, and self-heating are not experimentally covered.
why: Small scaling errors compound into large reactor-size and power predictions.
key_works: Garbet et al. (2010), *Gyrokinetic simulations of turbulent transport*, DOI: 10.1088/0029-5515/50/4/043002.

title: Kinetic validation of L–H threshold theory
subfield: Pedestals, confinement transitions, and density limits
open: Test whether first-principles L–H threshold predictions remain accurate with kinetic electrons, isotope mixtures, realistic neutrals, and different wall materials.
status: A 2026 preprint derives threshold, density-minimum, and field-asymmetry behavior in a flux-driven two-fluid framework; broader validation remains open.
why: Heating systems must cross the threshold reliably without being excessively oversized.
key_works: De Lucca et al. (2026), *The L-H transition in tokamaks: power threshold, density minimum and toroidal-field asymmetry*, arXiv:2605.00624.

title: L–H hysteresis and transition-path prediction
subfield: Pedestals, confinement transitions, and density limits
open: Predict forward and reverse transition thresholds, waiting times, and sensitivity to perturbation history rather than only an average threshold power.
status: Transition models have advanced, but operating-path dependence remains a separate control and validation problem.
why: Hysteresis determines whether a plant can remain in its efficient operating regime during disturbances.
key_works: De Lucca et al. (2026), *The L-H transition in tokamaks: power threshold, density minimum and toroidal-field asymmetry*, arXiv:2605.00624.

title: Pedestal-width prediction outside fitted regimes
subfield: Pedestals, confinement transitions, and density limits
open: Predict pedestal width and height for unfamiliar shaping, collisionality, isotope composition, and pressure profiles without device-specific retuning.
status: EPED provides an influential predictive framework; extrapolation beyond its validated regimes remains an active problem.
why: The pedestal strongly constrains total fusion performance.
key_works: Snyder et al. (2011), *A first-principles predictive model of the pedestal height and width*, *Nuclear Fusion* 51, 103016.

title: Pedestal electron-transport closure
subfield: Pedestals, confinement transitions, and density limits
open: Identify and quantitatively reproduce the mechanisms setting electron heat transport throughout the pedestal, including interactions among candidate instabilities.
status: Existing pedestal models constrain stability, but stability boundaries alone do not supply a complete transport closure.
why: Accurate electron profiles are needed to predict both core performance and edge stability.
key_works: Garbet et al. (2010), *Gyrokinetic simulations of turbulent transport*, DOI: 10.1088/0029-5515/50/4/043002; Snyder et al. (2011), EPED study.

title: Reactor-compatible ELM-free confinement
subfield: Pedestals, confinement transitions, and density limits
open: Demonstrate a stationary, high-performance regime without damaging edge-localized modes under reactor-like low torque, high density, and metallic-wall conditions.
status: Several ELM-free regimes exist experimentally; the complete reactor-compatible parameter combination is not established.
why: Large repetitive ELMs can destroy otherwise adequate divertor components.
key_works: Loarte et al. (2025), *Required R&D in existing fusion facilities to support the new baseline ITER Research Plan*, ITR-25-005.

title: Predictive resonant-magnetic-perturbation penetration
subfield: Pedestals, confinement transitions, and density limits
open: Predict the perturbation amplitude and spectrum needed for ELM suppression while including plasma screening, rotation, islands, and density loss.
status: RMP control is experimentally established in selected regimes; reliable extrapolation remains a stated ITER research need.
why: Incorrect penetration predictions can produce ineffective control or unacceptable confinement degradation.
key_works: Greenfield et al. (2023), *Report of the US ITER Research Program Research Needs Workshop*, arXiv:2303.12094.

title: Negative-triangularity burning-plasma compatibility
subfield: Pedestals, confinement transitions, and density limits
open: Demonstrate that negative triangularity retains its confinement and edge advantages with reactor-level self-heating, exhaust, fueling, and bootstrap-current requirements.
status: A 2024 MANTA pilot-plant study explores this route; a design study is not integrated burning-plasma evidence.
why: It could avoid reliance on conventional high-performance H-mode operation.
key_works: Rutherford et al., MANTA Collaboration (2024), *MANTA: A Negative-Triangularity NASEM-Compliant Fusion Pilot Plant*, arXiv:2405.20243.

title: Mechanistic density-limit prediction
subfield: Pedestals, confinement transitions, and density limits
open: Predict the density limit from coupled radiation, turbulence, neutral penetration, current-profile evolution, and detachment rather than a single empirical scaling.
status: Several mechanisms and operating exceptions are known; a universal predictive reactor criterion is not established.
why: Density is a powerful route to higher fusion power but can trigger collapse.
key_works: Krasheninnikov et al. (2016), *Divertor plasma detachment*, *Physics of Plasmas* 23, 055602; ITER research-needs reports.

title: Neutral–pedestal feedback
subfield: Pedestals, confinement transitions, and density limits
open: Predict how recycled and injected neutrals change pedestal fueling, rotation, electric fields, and turbulence under reactor wall and pumping conditions.
status: Neutral effects are represented in edge modeling, but integrated predictive validation remains incomplete.
why: Fueling cannot be designed independently of the confinement barrier.
key_works: Loarte et al. (2025), *Required R&D in existing fusion facilities to support the new baseline ITER Research Plan*, ITR-25-005.

title: Low-torque quiescent high-confinement operation
subfield: Pedestals, confinement transitions, and density limits
open: Establish whether quiescent high-confinement regimes can be maintained with the weak external torque and restricted actuator set of a reactor.
status: Relevant regimes exist in present machines; low-torque reactor extrapolation remains distinct from demonstrating the regime itself.
why: It could provide continuous edge exhaust without large ELMs.
key_works: Greenfield et al. (2023), *Report of the US ITER Research Program Research Needs Workshop*, arXiv:2303.12094.

title: Sawtooth-trigger prediction
subfield: Magnetohydrodynamic stability, disruptions, and runaway electrons
open: Predict sawtooth crash timing and post-crash profiles with energetic particles, two-fluid effects, and reconnection physics included.
status: Sawteeth are longstanding observations; complete crash prediction remains beyond a universal validated model.
why: Sawteeth can seed more dangerous instabilities and redistribute fusion products.
key_works: Chen and Zonca (2016), *Physics of Alfvén waves and energetic particles in burning plasmas*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.88.015008.

title: Neoclassical-tearing-mode seed threshold
subfield: Magnetohydrodynamic stability, disruptions, and runaway electrons
open: Predict the minimum perturbation that seeds a damaging neoclassical tearing mode under evolving reactor pressure and current profiles.
status: The 2006 review established the major framework; seed formation and extrapolation remain distinct from linear stability.
why: Avoiding a seed may require far less control power than suppressing a mature island.
key_works: La Haye (2006), *Neoclassical tearing modes and their control*, DOI: 10.1063/1.2180747.

title: Locked-mode avoidance with imperfect fields
subfield: Magnetohydrodynamic stability, disruptions, and runaway electrons
open: Determine tolerable error-field spectra and correction strategies across startup, ramp-up, burn, and shutdown, including uncertain plasma response.
status: Error-field correction is established, but a reactor-wide robust tolerance specification is not supplied by existing control demonstrations.
why: Small field errors can lock modes and precipitate disruptions.
key_works: Ariola and Pironti (2016), *Magnetic Control of Tokamak Plasmas*, DOI: 10.1007/978-3-319-29890-0.

title: Resistive-wall-mode control at low rotation
subfield: Magnetohydrodynamic stability, disruptions, and runaway electrons
open: Demonstrate reliable resistive-wall-mode stabilization with reactor-like rotation, sensor access, conducting structures, and actuator limits.
status: Feedback methods and experiments exist; reactor implementation couples unresolved physics and hardware constraints.
why: It determines whether attractive high-pressure operating points can be used safely.
key_works: Ariola and Pironti (2014), *Control of resistive wall modes in tokamak plasmas*; Ariola and Pironti (2016), *Magnetic Control of Tokamak Plasmas*.

title: Three-dimensional disruption-force prediction
subfield: Magnetohydrodynamic stability, disruptions, and runaway electrons
open: Predict asymmetric electromagnetic forces during vertical displacement and current quench, including conducting structures and uncertain current paths.
status: ITER disruption studies identify these loads as major design drivers; conservative margins remain substantial.
why: Underprediction can compromise vessel and support integrity.
key_works: Lehnen et al. (2015), *Disruptions in ITER and strategies for their control and mitigation*, DOI: 10.1016/j.jnucmat.2014.10.075.

title: Out-of-distribution disruption prediction
subfield: Magnetohydrodynamic stability, disruptions, and runaway electrons
open: Predict disruptions on new machines and unfamiliar operating regimes with calibrated warning times, missed-event rates, and false-alarm costs.
status: Deep learning demonstrated cross-device progress in 2019; reliable extrapolation to reactor conditions remains unresolved.
why: A predictor that fails on the first unfamiliar dangerous event is not a protection system.
key_works: Kates-Harbeck, Svyatkovskiy, and Tang (2019), *Predicting disruptive instabilities in controlled fusion plasmas through deep learning*, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-019-1116-4.

title: Shattered-pellet assimilation
subfield: Magnetohydrodynamic stability, disruptions, and runaway electrons
open: Predict and control how injected fragments ablate, penetrate, mix, and radiate during a disruption, including asymmetric deposition.
status: Shattered-pellet injection is a developed mitigation approach; reactor-scale assimilation remains an active validation need.
why: Injecting material is useful only if it reaches and cools the plasma as intended.
key_works: Lehnen et al. (2015), *Disruptions in ITER and strategies for their control and mitigation*, DOI: 10.1016/j.jnucmat.2014.10.075.

title: Disruption-radiation asymmetry
subfield: Magnetohydrodynamic stability, disruptions, and runaway electrons
open: Bound localized radiative loading during mitigation and develop injection geometries that avoid damaging toroidal or poloidal concentration.
status: Radiation is intentionally used to spread disruption energy; its nonuniformity remains a component-protection concern.
why: Converting thermal energy to radiation does not guarantee safe wall loading.
key_works: Loarte et al. (2025), *Required R&D in existing fusion facilities to support the new baseline ITER Research Plan*, ITR-25-005.

title: Runaway seed prediction during thermal quench
subfield: Magnetohydrodynamic stability, disruptions, and runaway electrons
open: Predict the runaway seed from hot-tail, Dreicer, radioactive, and externally driven sources during realistic rapid cooling.
status: The 2019 runaway review synthesizes these mechanisms; their combined reactor prediction remains uncertain.
why: A small seed can become a destructive relativistic-electron population.
key_works: Breizman et al. (2019), *Physics of runaway electrons in tokamaks*, DOI: 10.1088/1741-4326/ab1822.

title: Avalanche multiplication under mitigation
subfield: Magnetohydrodynamic stability, disruptions, and runaway electrons
open: Determine when injected material suppresses runaway production and when its effects on electric fields and partially ionized collisions increase avalanche multiplication.
status: Massive-material-injection effects were quantified in 2019 models; robust reactor prescriptions remain unsettled.
why: An apparently protective intervention can worsen another disruption hazard.
key_works: Hesslow et al. (2019), *Influence of massive material injection on avalanche runaway generation during tokamak disruptions*, DOI: 10.1088/1741-4326/ab26c2.

title: Benign termination of a mature runaway beam
subfield: Magnetohydrodynamic stability, disruptions, and runaway electrons
open: Remove a high-current runaway beam without concentrated wall damage, unacceptable electromagnetic loads, or secondary beam formation.
status: Runaway dynamics and mitigation strategies are extensively studied; a universally reliable reactor-scale termination method is not established.
why: Prevention alone is insufficient for a credible protection strategy.
key_works: Breizman et al. (2019), *Physics of runaway electrons in tokamaks*, DOI: 10.1088/1741-4326/ab1822; Ataeiseresht et al. (2023), *Runaway electrons and their interaction with tungsten wall*, DOI: 10.1038/s41598-023-48672-7.

title: Runaway-free startup
subfield: Magnetohydrodynamic stability, disruptions, and runaway electrons
open: Establish startup waveforms and fueling strategies that avoid runaway formation despite uncertain prefill, impurities, and wall conditions.
status: Startup runaway generation was modeled explicitly in 2022; avoiding it across realistic operational variability remains open.
why: Dangerous electron populations can arise before normal confinement is established.
key_works: Hoppe et al. (2022), *Runaway electron generation during tokamak start-up*, DOI: 10.1017/S002237782200054X; arXiv:2203.09900.

title: Reactor divertor heat-flux width
open: Determine the heat-flux width at reactor scale and reconcile empirical scaling with kinetic simulations and possible turbulence broadening.
status: Eich’s 2013 scaling extrapolated to roughly millimeter-scale ITER widths; this is an extrapolation, not a reactor measurement.
why: Width directly sets peak divertor heat flux.
key_works: Eich et al. (2013), *Scaling of the tokamak near the scrape-off layer H-mode power width and implications for ITER*, DOI: 10.1088/0029-5515/53/9/093031; Chang et al. (2017), *Gyrokinetic projection of the divertor heat-flux width from present tokamaks to ITER*.

title: Stable detachment-front control
open: Maintain a detached divertor without the radiation front entering the confined plasma, despite changes in power, fueling, and impurities.
status: Detachment is experimentally established; robust reactor control of its operating window remains unresolved.
why: Both insufficient and excessive detachment can end useful operation.
key_works: Leonard (2018), *Plasma detachment in divertor tokamaks*; Krasheninnikov et al. (2017), *Physics of ultimate detachment of a tokamak divertor plasma*.

title: Simultaneous reactor-grade confinement and detachment
open: Demonstrate compatible core performance and exhaust at reactor heat loads, impurity concentrations, density, and pulse duration.
status: Full detachment with improved core confinement was demonstrated in 2021; the remaining problem is reactor-condition integration, not first coexistence.
why: Separate successes in confinement and exhaust do not establish a working power plant.
key_works: Wang et al. (2021), *Integration of full divertor detachment with improved core confinement for fusion energy*, DOI: 10.1038/s41467-021-21645-y.

title: Filament-driven far-SOL loading
open: Predict intermittent particle and heat transport to first-wall regions far from the nominal strike point.
status: Filament measurements and density-shoulder studies exist; reliable reactor wall-load distributions remain uncertain.
why: Components outside the divertor may receive substantial unplanned exposure.
key_works: Kuang et al. (2019), *Plasma fluctuations in the scrape-off layer and at the divertor target in Alcator C-Mod and their relationship to divertor collisionality and density shoulder formation*.

title: Molecular reaction closure in detached plasmas
open: Measure and model molecular-assisted recombination, dissociation, charge exchange, and vibrational populations accurately enough to predict detachment.
status: Atomic-only descriptions are insufficient in important detached regimes; reaction and state-population uncertainties remain.
why: Incorrect chemistry produces incorrect particle and power balances.
key_works: Krasheninnikov et al. (2016), *Divertor plasma detachment*, *Physics of Plasmas* 23, 055602.

title: Inner–outer divertor asymmetry
open: Predict the division of heat and particles between divertor legs across magnetic-field direction, drifts, collisionality, and geometry.
status: Recent work has clarified mechanisms, including research reported by PPPL in 2026; a general reactor predictive capability remains broader.
why: One divertor leg can fail while average exhaust performance appears acceptable.
key_works: PPPL (2026), *Solving a mystery that could help fusion reactors survive decades of use*.

title: Advanced-divertor reactor scaling
open: Establish whether Super-X, snowflake, X-point-target, and related geometries retain their advantages under reactor constraints on coils, shielding, pumping, and control.
status: Advanced geometries have experimental and modeling support; full plant integration remains unresolved.
why: Geometric heat spreading may relax the most severe material requirements.
key_works: Leonard (2018), *Plasma detachment in divertor tokamaks*; NASEM (2021), *Bringing Fusion to the U.S. Grid*, DOI: 10.17226/25991.

title: Near-SOL heat-flux feature
open: Predict when a narrow near-SOL heat-flux component appears and suppress it without degrading useful confinement.
status: Impurity seeding was investigated as a suppression method in 2017; a general predictive criterion remains open.
why: A narrow additional component can dominate peak surface loading.
key_works: Nespoli et al. (2017), *Impurity seeding for suppression of the near Scrape-Off Layer heat flux feature in tokamaks*, arXiv:1712.00951.

title: Tungsten-source feedback through the edge
open: Predict and control the feedback among tungsten sputtering, impurity radiation, edge cooling, and further material release.
status: Plasma–material interaction studies document the constituent mechanisms; their integrated reactor feedback remains difficult.
why: A small initial contamination event can become self-amplifying.
key_works: Federici et al. (2001), *Plasma-material interactions in current tokamaks and their implications for next step fusion reactors*, DOI: 10.1088/0029-5515/41/12/218.

title: Neutral residence and exhaust efficiency
open: Predict how divertor geometry, molecular kinetics, conductance, and pumping determine fuel residence time and helium removal.
status: Exhaust models and pumping technologies exist; their simultaneous optimization with detachment and tritium inventory remains unresolved.
why: Poor exhaust increases fuel inventory and can destabilize the burn.
key_works: Day and Giegerich (2014), *Development of Advanced Exhaust Pumping Technology for a DT Fusion Power Plant*, DOI: 10.1109/TPS.2014.2307435.

title: Exhaust control with finite actuator delays
open: Design a controller that respects gas-delivery, impurity-transport, diagnostic, and magnetic-actuator delays while avoiding dangerous detachment excursions.
status: Detachment physics is mature enough for control development, but reactor delay and reliability requirements remain unproven.
why: A physically controllable regime may still be operationally inaccessible with slow hardware.
key_works: Leonard (2018), *Plasma detachment in divertor tokamaks*; Ariola and Pironti (2016), *Magnetic Control of Tokamak Plasmas*.

title: Protective vapor shielding without plasma poisoning
open: Determine whether a material-vapor layer can reproducibly shield surfaces during transients without unacceptable contamination, radiation collapse, or erosion.
status: Vapor shielding is part of longstanding plasma–material interaction research; useful repetitive reactor operation is not established.
why: It could soften transient material loads, but may introduce a new failure mechanism.
key_works: Federici et al. (2001), *Plasma-material interactions in current tokamaks and their implications for next step fusion reactors*, DOI: 10.1088/0029-5515/41/12/218.

title: Electron-cyclotron deposition accuracy
open: Maintain precise heating and current-drive deposition despite density fluctuations, refraction, evolving equilibrium, and diagnostic uncertainty.
status: Electron-cyclotron control is established; reactor requirements tighten the tolerances on location and reliability.
why: Misaligned current drive can fail to suppress a magnetic island.
key_works: Prater (2004), *Heating and current drive by electron cyclotron waves*, DOI: 10.1063/1.1690762; Welander et al. (2013), *Advanced control of neoclassical tearing modes in DIII-D with real-time steering of the electron cyclotron current drive*.

title: Reactor-duty gyrotron systems
open: Qualify efficient high-power gyrotrons, windows, transmission lines, and launchers for the continuous duty and availability required by a power plant.
status: High-power electron-cyclotron systems exist; plant-wide efficiency and lifetime remain distinct qualification problems.
why: Heating-system inefficiency directly subtracts from net electricity.
key_works: Prater (2004), *Heating and current drive by electron cyclotron waves*, DOI: 10.1063/1.1690762; Loarte et al. (2025), ITR-25-005.

title: High-density lower-hybrid current drive
open: Demonstrate efficient lower-hybrid current drive at reactor density and temperature while controlling edge losses, spectral evolution, and accessibility.
status: Current-drive theory and experiments are longstanding; reactor-compatible efficiency is not established by general theory alone.
why: Efficient noninductive current drive is essential for many steady-state tokamak designs.
key_works: Fisch (1987), *Theory of current drive in plasmas*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.59.175; ITER research-needs workshop (2023), arXiv:2303.12094.

title: Ion-cyclotron sheath and impurity control
open: Predict and suppress radio-frequency sheath voltages and resulting impurity release around ion-cyclotron antennas under reactor conditions.
status: Ion-cyclotron heating is established; antenna–edge–wall coupling remains a research requirement.
why: An effective heating method can become unusable if it contaminates the plasma.
key_works: Loarte et al. (2025), *Required R&D in existing fusion facilities to support the new baseline ITER Research Plan*, ITR-25-005.

title: Reliable negative-ion neutral-beam sources
open: Sustain reactor-duty negative-ion production with controlled cesium behavior, stable optics, low electron co-extraction, and acceptable maintenance.
status: Negative-ion technology underpins advanced neutral beams; reactor availability and long-duration surface control remain qualification gaps.
why: Beam-source maintenance can dominate heating-system downtime.
key_works: Greenfield et al. (2023), *Report of the US ITER Research Program Research Needs Workshop*, arXiv:2303.12094.

title: Efficient neutralization beyond gas cells
open: Demonstrate a neutralization architecture, such as photoneutralization, whose complete electrical efficiency and reliability materially improve reactor neutral beams.
status: Alternative neutralization is a development route rather than an established power-plant subsystem.
why: Neutralization losses can make otherwise useful beam heating too expensive energetically.
key_works: NASEM (2021), *Bringing Fusion to the U.S. Grid*, DOI: 10.17226/25991; Fisch (1987), *Theory of current drive in plasmas*.

title: Deep pellet fueling of hot plasmas
open: Predict and achieve sufficient pellet penetration and fuel deposition in reactor-temperature plasmas without unacceptable edge disturbances.
status: Pellet fueling is established; hotter plasmas and stringent tritium-efficiency requirements change the optimization problem.
why: Gas fueling alone may not provide the desired core density efficiently.
key_works: Abdou et al. (2021), *Physics and technology considerations for the deuterium–tritium fuel cycle and conditions for tritium fuel self sufficiency*, DOI: 10.1088/1741-4326/abbf35.

title: High-availability tritium pellet production
open: Produce, accelerate, route, and inject tritium-bearing pellets continuously with low inventory, low failure rate, and remote maintainability.
status: Experimental pellet systems exist; power-plant throughput and lifecycle qualification remain open.
why: Fuel delivery must function as industrial equipment rather than an experimental accessory.
key_works: Glugla et al. (2023 report), *Tritium Technology for Fusion Devices—Status and R&D Needs*, UKAEA-CCFE-PR(23)99.

title: Noninductive current ramp to steady state
open: Reach and maintain the required current profile using bootstrap and externally driven current without relying on unsustainable transformer flux.
status: Noninductive scenarios have substantial research history; an integrated reactor ramp with acceptable power demand remains unproven.
why: Steady-state operation requires more than a steady-state equilibrium calculation.
key_works: Fisch (1987), *Theory of current drive in plasmas*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.59.175; Greenfield et al. (2023), arXiv:2303.12094.

title: Exact global nonaxisymmetric quasisymmetry
open: Prove existence or an appropriate impossibility theorem for globally toroidal, nonaxisymmetric, physically admissible equilibria with exact quasisymmetry.
status: Extremely precise numerical quasisymmetry was demonstrated in 2022; September 2026 work still explicitly identifies exact nonaxisymmetric quasisymmetric equilibria as open.
why: It would establish the mathematical limits of a central stellarator design principle.
key_works: Landreman and Paul (2022), *Magnetic Fields with Precise Quasisymmetry for Plasma Confinement*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.128.035001; Landreman (2026), arXiv:2609.26742.

title: Exact three-dimensional vacuum equilibria with nested surfaces
open: Construct exact analytic, nonaxisymmetric toroidal vacuum fields with nested toroidal flux surfaces, or prove precisely stated obstructions.
status: September 2026 analytic finite-pressure constructions do not settle the curl-free case; the paper explicitly leaves it open.
why: Exact examples would test equilibrium codes and clarify what external coils can realize.
key_works: Landreman (2026), *Analytic toroidal 3D MHD equilibria and steady Euler flows with invariant surfaces*, arXiv:2609.26742.

title: Exact force-free toroidal equilibria with nested surfaces
open: Determine whether exact analytic nonaxisymmetric force-free toroidal fields can possess the desired nested-surface structure.
status: Explicitly unresolved in the September 2026 analytic-equilibrium paper; it is distinct from the newly constructed finite-pressure families.
why: It connects stellarator geometry to current-carrying low-pressure equilibria.
key_works: Landreman (2026), *Analytic toroidal 3D MHD equilibria and steady Euler flows with invariant surfaces*, arXiv:2609.26742.

title: Robustness of smooth three-dimensional equilibria
open: Characterize which perturbations of pressure, boundary shape, or current preserve smooth nested-surface equilibria and which generate islands or singular structures.
status: September 2026 preprints report counterexamples to formulations of Grad’s conjecture; existence of examples does not establish generic robustness.
why: A mathematically exact but structurally fragile equilibrium may be unusable in a machine.
key_works: Gómez-Serrano, Liehr, and Taylor (2026), *Counterexamples to Grad’s conjecture*, arXiv:2609.24739.

title: From local Boozer fields to global reactors
open: Determine which locally realizable field-strength functions extend to globally toroidal, force-balanced fields generated by acceptable coils.
status: Klotz et al. reported a local realization result in September 2026; global topology, equilibrium, and coil realizability remain additional conditions.
why: Local freedom can otherwise be mistaken for unrestricted reactor-design freedom.
key_works: Klotz et al. (2026), *All field strengths are possible locally in Boozer coordinates*, arXiv:2609.09517.

title: Analyticity versus omnigenity
open: Quantify the transport penalty introduced when ideal omnigenous constructions are approximated by smooth, manufacturable magnetic fields.
status: Cary and Shasharina’s 1997 analysis established subtle relationships among omnigenity, quasihelicity, and analyticity; practical approximation limits remain important.
why: Exact confinement properties may degrade under the smoothing needed for physical coils.
key_works: Cary and Shasharina (1997), *Omnigenity and quasihelicity in helical plasma confinement systems*, DOI: 10.1063/1.872473.

title: Piecewise-omnigenous collisional transport
open: Determine the collisional and finite-orbit-width transport generated at transitions between approximately omnigenous regions.
status: Generalized omnigenity and newer optimization methods enlarge the design space; realistic transport across their boundaries needs validation.
why: Good collisionless orbits need not imply acceptable thermal transport.
key_works: *Magnetic Fields with General Omnigenity* (2024 version), arXiv:2305.08026; *Optimizing omnigenity like quasisymmetry for stellarators* (2025), arXiv:2502.09350.

title: Near-axis expansion error bounds
open: Develop useful, computable bounds on how accurately near-axis constructions represent finite-volume fields, surfaces, and confinement properties.
status: Near-axis methods are powerful design tools, but finite-radius utility is not guaranteed by a local expansion alone.
why: Certified error estimates would prevent optimization around asymptotically attractive but impractical configurations.
key_works: Garren and Boozer (1991), *Existence of quasihelically symmetric stellarators*, *Physics of Fluids B* 3, 2822; Klotz et al. (2026), arXiv:2609.09517.

title: Coil-complexity lower bounds
open: Establish lower bounds or sharp tradeoffs among field accuracy, coil curvature, coil separation, conductor length, and access requirements.
status: Optimization produces good designs, including finite-element-aware work in 2026; it does not establish global limits.
why: Bounds could identify when a proposed plasma shape is intrinsically expensive to realize.
key_works: Kaptanoglu and Gil (2026), *A proof-of-concept for automated AI-driven stellarator coil optimization with in-the-loop finite-element calculations*, arXiv:2603.15240.

title: Joint confinement–stability–engineering optimization
open: Find robust stellarator configurations that simultaneously satisfy transport, energetic-particle, MHD, coil-stress, shielding, and maintenance constraints.
status: Individual objectives and some coupled optimizations exist; a validated full reactor Pareto frontier does not.
why: Optimizing one metric can silently make another subsystem infeasible.
key_works: Helander (2014), *Theory of plasma confinement in non-axisymmetric magnetic fields*, DOI: 10.1088/0034-4885/77/8/087001; Kaptanoglu and Gil (2026), arXiv:2603.15240.

title: Symmetry-agnostic confinement design
open: Validate whether iso-action and related non-quasisymmetric design principles yield robust thermal and energetic-particle confinement with realistic collisions and coils.
status: Sengupta, Bhattacharjee, and Buller proposed a general theory in August 2026; reactor validation remains open.
why: It may reveal good configurations excluded by conventional symmetry constraints.
key_works: Sengupta et al. (2026), *Symmetry-agnostic stellarators for collisionless confinement*, arXiv:2608.20042.

title: Experimental reactor-alpha confinement in optimized stellarators
open: Demonstrate sufficiently low energetic-particle losses in an optimized stellarator under self-consistent high-pressure conditions.
status: Orbit optimization can substantially reduce calculated losses; burning-plasma experimental validation remains absent from those design results.
why: Alpha confinement is necessary for both self-heating and wall survival.
key_works: Landreman and Paul (2022), *Magnetic Fields with Precise Quasisymmetry for Plasma Confinement*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.128.035001; IAEA energetic-particle optimization contributions (2021).

title: Turbulence-optimized stellarators
open: Demonstrate that reducing calculated turbulent transport produces reproducible confinement improvement without sacrificing neoclassical or engineering performance.
status: Wendelstein 7-X demonstrated reduced neoclassical transport in 2021; turbulent transport is a separate optimization frontier.
why: Solving neoclassical transport alone does not guarantee reactor confinement.
key_works: Beidler et al. (2021), *Demonstration of reduced neoclassical energy transport in Wendelstein 7-X*, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-021-03687-w.

title: Stellarator impurity screening at high density
open: Establish high-density operating regimes that avoid impurity accumulation while maintaining good confinement and manageable exhaust.
status: Stellarator neoclassical theory identifies strong electric-field and collisionality dependence; the reactor operating window remains unresolved.
why: High-charge impurity accumulation can negate the advantages of steady-state confinement.
key_works: Helander (2014), *Theory of plasma confinement in non-axisymmetric magnetic fields*, DOI: 10.1088/0034-4885/77/8/087001.

title: High-beta stellarator stability margins
open: Determine experimentally reliable pressure limits including nonlinear MHD activity, equilibrium changes, islands, and energetic particles.
status: Stellarator stability and equilibrium theory are mature research areas, but reactor-pressure margins remain configuration-dependent.
why: Pressure limits directly influence reactor size and magnet requirements.
key_works: Helander (2014), *Theory of plasma confinement in non-axisymmetric magnetic fields*, DOI: 10.1088/0034-4885/77/8/087001.

title: Bootstrap-current and transform robustness
open: Keep rotational transform and island topology within acceptable limits as bootstrap current changes during startup, fueling, heating, and burn.
status: Optimized configurations can reduce sensitivity, but operating trajectories still couple transport to equilibrium.
why: A nominally current-free concept can still experience consequential plasma-generated currents.
key_works: Beidler et al. (2021), *Demonstration of reduced neoclassical energy transport in Wendelstein 7-X*, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-021-03687-w; Helander (2014).

title: Reactor island-divertor exhaust
open: Demonstrate an island-divertor configuration with adequate heat spreading, pumping, impurity control, and tolerance to equilibrium changes at reactor power.
status: Island divertors are implemented experimentally; reactor-level exhaust integration remains open.
why: Stellarators exchange tokamak-specific challenges for a different three-dimensional exhaust problem.
key_works: NASEM (2021), *Bringing Fusion to the U.S. Grid*, DOI: 10.17226/25991; Helander (2014), DOI: 10.1088/0034-4885/77/8/087001.

title: As-built coil-error certification
open: Convert coil metrology, assembly tolerances, thermal deformation, and electromagnetic loading into certified bounds on confinement degradation.
status: Accurate coil designs and mechanical optimization exist; end-to-end uncertainty certification remains a separate problem.
why: The plasma experiences the loaded, assembled coils—not the ideal CAD model.
key_works: Kaptanoglu and Gil (2026), *A proof-of-concept for automated AI-driven stellarator coil optimization with in-the-loop finite-element calculations*, arXiv:2603.15240.

title: Maintainable stellarator coil and blanket geometry
open: Demonstrate a stellarator architecture permitting timely blanket and divertor replacement without unacceptable degradation of magnetic performance.
status: Coil optimization has advanced substantially; reactor maintenance access remains an independent integration constraint.
why: Excellent confinement is commercially insufficient if activated components cannot be replaced efficiently.
key_works: NASEM (2021), *Bringing Fusion to the U.S. Grid*, DOI: 10.17226/25991; Crofts and Harman (2014), arXiv:1412.4008.

title: Solenoid-free spherical-tokamak startup
subfield: Spherical tokamaks, reversed-field pinches, spheromaks, and mirrors
open: Produce a reactor-relevant spherical-tokamak current and closed-flux configuration without a conventional central solenoid.
status: Alternative startup methods exist, but the complete reactor trajectory remains a development problem.
why: The narrow center column leaves little space for startup hardware and shielding.
key_works: Menard et al. (2016), *Fusion nuclear science facilities and pilot plants based on the spherical tokamak*, DOI: 10.1088/0029-5515/56/10/106023.

title: Spherical-tokamak center-column lifetime
subfield: Spherical tokamaks, reversed-field pinches, spheromaks, and mirrors
open: Achieve an acceptable center-column lifetime while accommodating neutron shielding, structural loads, cooling, and magnetic-field requirements.
status: The tradeoff is explicit in spherical-tokamak pilot studies; integrated lifetime qualification remains open.
why: Center-column replacement can erase the economic advantages of compactness.
key_works: Menard et al. (2016), *Fusion nuclear science facilities and pilot plants based on the spherical tokamak*, DOI: 10.1088/0029-5515/56/10/106023.

title: Burning-plasma single-helical-axis RFP operation
subfield: Spherical tokamaks, reversed-field pinches, spheromaks, and mirrors
open: Sustain the favorable single-helical-axis reversed-field-pinch state at fusion-relevant temperature, density, and self-heating.
status: Self-organized helical equilibria were demonstrated by 2009; reactor-grade confinement is a separate unresolved target.
why: It could enable a lower-field confinement route.
key_works: Lorenzini et al. (2009), *Self-organized helical equilibria as a new paradigm for ohmically heated fusion plasmas*, DOI: 10.1038/nphys1308.

title: Low-loss RFP sustainment
subfield: Spherical tokamaks, reversed-field pinches, spheromaks, and mirrors
open: Sustain the reversed-field-pinch current and magnetic configuration with acceptable recirculating power and controlled stochastic transport.
status: RFP self-organization and boundary structure are experimentally studied; economical sustained fusion operation is not established.
why: Low magnet requirements are not useful if plasma sustainment consumes excessive power.
key_works: Martines et al. (2009), *The plasma boundary in Single Helical Axis RFP plasmas*, arXiv:0909.3011; Lorenzini et al. (2009), DOI: 10.1038/nphys1308.

title: Spheromak helicity injection without confinement loss
subfield: Spherical tokamaks, reversed-field pinches, spheromaks, and mirrors
open: Sustain a spheromak while injecting magnetic helicity without introducing transport or impurities that prevent fusion gain.
status: Relaxation theory and helicity-driven configurations are longstanding; sustainment and good confinement remain difficult to combine.
why: It tests whether simple coil geometry can coexist with adequate plasma performance.
key_works: Taylor (1986), *Relaxation and magnetic reconnection in plasmas*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.58.741; Light et al. (2025), *Counterintuitive Particle Confinement In A Helical Force-Free Plasma*, DOI: 10.3390/plasma8020020.

title: Predictive reconnection heating in compact tori
subfield: Spherical tokamaks, reversed-field pinches, spheromaks, and mirrors
open: Predict the partition of reconnection energy among ions, electrons, bulk motion, and escaping particles during compact-torus formation or merging.
status: Reconnection-based heating is experimentally investigated; a transferable reactor-design closure remains unavailable.
why: Formation energy is useful only if it becomes confined fuel heat.
key_works: Taylor (1986), *Relaxation and magnetic reconnection in plasmas*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.58.741; Steinhauer (2011), *Review of field-reversed configurations*, DOI: 10.1063/1.3613680.

title: Gas-dynamic-trap end-loss reduction
subfield: Spherical tokamaks, reversed-field pinches, spheromaks, and mirrors
open: Reduce axial energy loss enough for a useful fusion system while retaining stable, accessible mirror operation.
status: Gas-dynamic-trap experiments and models were comprehensively reviewed in 2013; power-plant energy balance remains unresolved.
why: Open field lines create a loss channel absent from closed toroidal confinement.
key_works: Ivanov and Prikhodko (2013), *Gas-dynamic trap: an overview of the concept and experimental results*, *Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion* 55, 063001.

title: Economical tandem-mirror barriers
subfield: Spherical tokamaks, reversed-field pinches, spheromaks, and mirrors
open: Sustain end-plug or thermal-barrier potentials with a complete auxiliary-power requirement compatible with net fusion electricity.
status: Mirror confinement concepts are longstanding; useful barriers must be assessed together with their creation and maintenance costs.
why: A barrier that saves plasma energy but consumes more electrical energy does not solve the plant problem.
key_works: Ivanov and Prikhodko (2013), *Gas-dynamic trap: an overview of the concept and experimental results*; Wurzel and Hsu (2022), DOI: 10.1063/5.0083990.

title: Simultaneous mirror microstability and MHD stability
subfield: Spherical tokamaks, reversed-field pinches, spheromaks, and mirrors
open: Find mirror distributions that suppress loss-cone and other kinetic instabilities while also satisfying macroscopic interchange stability.
status: Stabilization mechanisms exist individually; a reactor-quality combined window remains unresolved.
why: Fixing one instability can worsen another or increase end losses.
key_works: Ivanov and Prikhodko (2013), *Gas-dynamic trap: an overview of the concept and experimental results*.

title: Mirror end-loss energy recovery
subfield: Spherical tokamaks, reversed-field pinches, spheromaks, and mirrors
open: Recover a useful fraction of escaping charged-particle energy while accommodating broad distributions, secondary electrons, impurities, and neutron exposure.
status: Direct-conversion concepts exist; an integrated reactor-duty system remains unqualified.
why: Recovery could turn a confinement disadvantage into a partly useful energy stream.
key_works: Wurzel and Hsu (2025), *Continuing progress toward fusion energy breakeven and gain as measured against the Lawson criteria*, arXiv:2505.03834.

title: FRC electron-energy confinement
subfield: Field-reversed configurations, Z pinches, cusps, and dipoles
open: Establish electron heat-confinement scaling in field-reversed configurations at reactor-relevant temperatures and size.
status: The 2011 review identifies transport as central; subsequent formation and sustainment progress does not independently settle reactor electron losses.
why: Rapid electron losses can prevent gain despite favorable ion behavior.
key_works: Steinhauer (2011), *Review of field-reversed configurations*, DOI: 10.1063/1.3613680.

title: Positive FRC beam-sustainment balance
subfield: Field-reversed configurations, Z pinches, cusps, and dipoles
open: Demonstrate that neutral-beam-maintained FRC fusion output can exceed the complete power required to sustain the configuration.
status: Beam-generated FRCs were reported in 2025; formation itself is therefore not the open problem.
why: Strong beam support can improve confinement while masking an unfavorable power balance.
key_works: Roche et al. (2025), *Generation of field-reversed configurations via neutral beam injection*, DOI: 10.1038/s41467-025-58849-5.

title: Kinetic stabilization of reactor-scale FRCs
subfield: Field-reversed configurations, Z pinches, cusps, and dipoles
open: Predict whether favorable finite-orbit and energetic-ion stabilization persists as FRC size, collisionality, and fusion-product populations change.
status: High-performance beam-supported FRC states exist; reactor-scale stability remains an extrapolation.
why: Stabilization observed in one kinetic regime may not survive scaling.
key_works: Steinhauer (2011), *Review of field-reversed configurations*; Roche et al. (2025), DOI: 10.1038/s41467-025-58849-5.

title: FRC merging and compression efficiency
subfield: Field-reversed configurations, Z pinches, cusps, and dipoles
open: Measure and optimize retained flux, particle inventory, and thermal energy through formation, translation, merging, and compression.
status: These processes are established research techniques; their cumulative reactor-cycle efficiency remains unresolved.
why: Modest losses at each stage can eliminate total-cycle gain.
key_works: Steinhauer (2011), *Review of field-reversed configurations*, DOI: 10.1063/1.3613680; Ellison et al. (2024), arXiv:2408.15206.

title: Sheared-flow Z-pinch scaling to gain
subfield: Field-reversed configurations, Z pinches, cusps, and dipoles
open: Demonstrate that shear-flow stabilization survives at the density, temperature, current, and duration required for fusion gain.
status: Sustained neutron production and thermonuclear-origin measurements exist; these do not establish reactor gain.
why: It tests a potentially simple, magnet-light confinement architecture.
key_works: Shumlak (2020), *Z-pinch fusion*, *Journal of Applied Physics* 127, 200901; Mitrani et al. (2021), DOI: 10.1063/5.0066257.

title: Unambiguous Z-pinch fusion-source attribution
subfield: Field-reversed configurations, Z pinches, cusps, and dipoles
open: Establish robust diagnostics that distinguish bulk thermonuclear fusion from beam–target contributions throughout scaling campaigns.
status: Mitrani et al. demonstrated relevant discrimination in 2021; extending it across devices and higher-performance regimes remains necessary.
why: Neutron yield alone can misrepresent fuel temperature and prospects for gain.
key_works: Mitrani et al. (2021), *Thermonuclear neutron emission from a sheared-flow stabilized Z-pinch*, DOI: 10.1063/5.0066257.

title: Repetitive dense-plasma-focus operation
subfield: Field-reversed configurations, Z pinches, cusps, and dipoles
open: Determine whether dense-plasma-focus systems can achieve reproducible useful fusion performance while controlling electrode erosion, impurities, and shot-to-shot variability.
status: Pinch fusion has a long experimental history; repetitive energy-system qualification remains unresolved.
why: A high-yield isolated shot is not a repeatable industrial process.
key_works: Shumlak (2020), *Z-pinch fusion*, *Journal of Applied Physics* 127, 200901; Wurzel and Hsu (2022), DOI: 10.1063/5.0083990.

title: High-beta cusp confinement with full power balance
subfield: Field-reversed configurations, Z pinches, cusps, and dipoles
open: Demonstrate simultaneous electron and ion confinement, useful fusion reactivity, and acceptable injection losses in a high-beta cusp system.
status: Enhanced high-energy-electron confinement was demonstrated in 2015; complete fusion gain was not.
why: Electron confinement is necessary but insufficient for cusp-based fusion.
key_works: Park et al. (2015), *High-Energy Electron Confinement in a Magnetic Cusp Configuration*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevX.5.021024.

title: Fusion-relevant levitated-dipole confinement
subfield: Field-reversed configurations, Z pinches, cusps, and dipoles
open: Establish high-temperature ion confinement, fueling, stability, and coil survivability in a levitated dipole at useful fusion conditions.
status: Turbulent inward particle pinch was demonstrated in 2010; reactor energy confinement and engineering remain open.
why: Dipoles offer a qualitatively different confinement topology.
key_works: Boxer et al. (2010), *Turbulent inward pinch of plasma confined by a levitated dipole magnet*, DOI: 10.1038/nphys1510; Kobayashi et al. (2009), DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.103.055003.

title: Generalized IEC power-balance bounds
subfield: Field-reversed configurations, Z pinches, cusps, and dipoles
open: Establish rigorous power-balance limits for precisely defined inertial-electrostatic-confinement architectures, including proposed mechanisms that depart from standard assumptions.
status: Important restricted loss arguments already exist; simply restating them is not an open problem.
why: Strong bounds can eliminate unproductive designs or identify genuinely different regimes.
key_works: Rider (1995), *A general critique of inertial-electrostatic confinement fusion systems*, DOI: 10.1063/1.871273; Rider (1997), DOI: 10.1063/1.872556.

title: High-gain magnetized-liner fusion
subfield: Magnetized inertial fusion and pulsed power
open: Demonstrate magnetized-liner target gain sufficient for a credible complete-system power balance, not merely favorable pressure–confinement products.
status: Magnetized pulsed approaches have substantial experimental progress; the 2024 opportunities paper advocates further development rather than reporting a power plant.
why: It is the central performance discriminator for this fusion family.
key_works: Ellison et al. (2024), *Opportunities in Pulsed Magnetic Fusion Energy*, arXiv:2408.15206.

title: Nonlinear magneto-Rayleigh–Taylor control
subfield: Magnetized inertial fusion and pulsed power
open: Predict and suppress liner instability through nonlinear growth, mode coupling, material strength changes, and stagnation.
status: Instability physics is extensively studied; acceptable perturbation growth at high-gain conditions remains a limiting issue.
why: Small liner imperfections can become fuel contamination or asymmetric compression.
key_works: Hurricane et al. (2023), *Physics principles of inertial confinement fusion and U.S. program overview*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.95.025005.

title: Magnetic-flux retention during compression
subfield: Magnetized inertial fusion and pulsed power
open: Predict and control flux loss from resistivity, Nernst transport, reconnection, and multidimensional motion during magnetized implosion.
status: Magnetized-target models include these effects, but their combined quantitative validation remains incomplete.
why: Compressed magnetic fields are useful only if they remain coupled to the hot fuel.
key_works: Ellison et al. (2024), *Opportunities in Pulsed Magnetic Fusion Energy*, arXiv:2408.15206.

title: Uniform magnetized-fuel preheat
subfield: Magnetized inertial fusion and pulsed power
open: Deposit preheat energy in the fuel with sufficiently low nonuniformity, wall interaction, and impurity production.
status: Preheat is a demonstrated ingredient of magnetized-liner approaches; efficient high-gain integration remains open.
why: Poor preheat can increase required compression or seed destructive asymmetry.
key_works: Hurricane et al. (2023), *Physics principles of inertial confinement fusion and U.S. program overview*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.95.025005.

title: Axial end-loss closure in magnetized targets
subfield: Magnetized inertial fusion and pulsed power
open: Quantify and suppress particle and thermal losses through target ends without creating unacceptable preheat, injection, or manufacturing penalties.
status: End losses are part of magnetized-target design studies; a robust reactor target solution remains unresolved.
why: Radial insulation does not solve losses along magnetic field lines.
key_works: Ellison et al. (2024), *Opportunities in Pulsed Magnetic Fusion Energy*, arXiv:2408.15206.

title: Liner-material mix prediction
subfield: Magnetized inertial fusion and pulsed power
open: Predict contamination of the fusion fuel from liner interfaces and determine manufacturing tolerances that keep radiation losses acceptable.
status: Mixing is recognized across inertial-fusion approaches; predictive multiscale treatment remains difficult.
why: A small mass of high-charge material can strongly cool compressed fuel.
key_works: Zhou, Sadler, and Hurricane (2025), *Instabilities and Mixing in Inertial Confinement Fusion*, DOI: 10.1146/annurev-fluid-022824-110008.

title: Pulsed-power current delivery at scale
subfield: Magnetized inertial fusion and pulsed power
open: Deliver the intended current waveform to the imploding load while controlling plasma formation, insulation breakdown, current loss, and electrode damage.
status: Large pulsed-power facilities demonstrate substantial capability; reactor repetition and efficient scaling remain unresolved.
why: Stored electrical energy is irrelevant if it does not reach the target in the required waveform.
key_works: Ellison et al. (2024), *Opportunities in Pulsed Magnetic Fusion Energy*, arXiv:2408.15206.

title: Repetitive pulser energy recovery
subfield: Magnetized inertial fusion and pulsed power
open: Recover unused magnetic and electrical energy over repeated fusion cycles without sacrificing pulse quality or component lifetime.
status: Energy recovery is an attractive systems objective; integrated fusion-duty validation is not established.
why: Recovery can determine whether a pulsed concept has acceptable recirculating power.
key_works: Ellison et al. (2024), *Opportunities in Pulsed Magnetic Fusion Energy*, arXiv:2408.15206; DOE (2026), *Fusion Science and Technology Roadmap*.

title: Symmetric liquid-piston compression
subfield: Magnetized inertial fusion and pulsed power
open: Compress magnetized plasma with a liquid or mechanically driven liner while controlling synchronization errors, jets, shocks, and plasma contamination.
status: Magneto-inertial architectures are included in gain surveys; repeatable high-gain compression remains an experimental discriminator.
why: Mechanical drivers could reduce cost but introduce difficult hydrodynamic tolerances.
key_works: Wurzel and Hsu (2025), *Continuing progress toward fusion energy breakeven and gain as measured against the Lawson criteria*, arXiv:2505.03834.

title: Plasma-jet liner assembly
subfield: Magnetized inertial fusion and pulsed power
open: Merge many plasma jets into a sufficiently uniform, low-entropy imploding liner with acceptable mass, momentum, and timing variation.
status: Plasma-liner concepts have an established research history; high-gain target compression remains unresolved.
why: A standoff driver could protect hardware from the fusion chamber.
key_works: Wurzel and Hsu (2022), *Progress toward fusion energy breakeven and gain as measured against the Lawson criterion*, DOI: 10.1063/5.0083990.

title: Robust high target gain
open: Achieve high target gain with a broad tolerance margin against realistic driver and target variations.
status: LLNL reported 8.6 ± 0.45 MJ from 2.08 MJ laser input in 2025, and still cited 8.6 MJ in May 2026; this establishes gain, not industrial robustness.
why: A power plant needs repeatable gain, not occasional exceptional shots.
key_works: Abu-Shawareb et al. (2024), *Achievement of Target Gain Larger than Unity in an Inertial Fusion Experiment*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.132.065102; LLNL reports, 2025–2026.

title: Low-mode implosion asymmetry prediction
open: Predict the effect of low-order shape and drive asymmetries on stagnation, residual motion, and burn, with experimentally validated uncertainty.
status: Asymmetry control helped enable ignition; predictive tolerance across target families remains open.
why: A small global asymmetry can prevent otherwise adequate compression.
key_works: Betti and Hurricane (2016), *Inertial-confinement fusion with lasers*, DOI: 10.1038/nphys3736; Hurricane et al. (2023), DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.95.025005.

title: Ablative Rayleigh–Taylor prediction across scales
open: Predict instability growth from manufacturing-scale perturbations through nonlinear saturation and burn-relevant mixing.
status: Linear and nonlinear models are well developed; complete predictive multiscale closure remains difficult.
why: The allowable target roughness depends on the entire instability cascade.
key_works: Zhou, Sadler, and Hurricane (2025), *Instabilities and Mixing in Inertial Confinement Fusion*, DOI: 10.1146/annurev-fluid-022824-110008.

title: Defect-induced mix tolerance
open: Quantify acceptable capsule defects, supports, fill-tube perturbations, and inclusions using validated three-dimensional burn predictions.
status: Defect control has materially improved implosions; a broad industrial tolerance specification remains unresolved.
why: Target manufacturing cost depends strongly on what imperfections can be tolerated.
key_works: Zhou et al. (2025), *Instabilities and Mixing in Inertial Confinement Fusion*, DOI: 10.1146/annurev-fluid-022824-110008.

title: Rapid, uniform cryogenic fuel layering
open: Form deuterium–tritium ice layers with the required thickness and roughness at industrial throughput, and preserve them until implosion.
status: Precision cryogenic layering exists for experiments; high-throughput inexpensive production remains a stated IFE need.
why: Laboratory preparation methods may be incompatible with millions of targets.
key_works: Ma (2023), *Priority Research Opportunities from the 2022 DOE Basic Research Needs for Inertial Fusion Energy*.

title: Multispecies kinetic effects in hot spots
open: Quantify species separation, non-Maxwellian distributions, and kinetic transport during ignition-scale implosions.
status: Hydrodynamic models explain much performance, but kinetic corrections can alter inferred temperature and reactivity.
why: A single-fluid temperature may not correctly determine fusion burn.
key_works: Betti and Hurricane (2016), *Inertial-confinement fusion with lasers*, DOI: 10.1038/nphys3736.

title: Nonlocal electron heat flow in implosions
open: Develop a computationally practical electron-transport model that remains accurate across steep gradients, changing collisionality, and magnetization.
status: Flux limits and kinetic calculations are used; a universally reliable reduced closure remains unavailable.
why: Heat flow affects ablation, shock timing, hot-spot formation, and ignition.
key_works: Craxton et al. (2015), *Direct-drive inertial confinement fusion: A review*, DOI: 10.1063/1.4934714.

title: Alpha stopping in burning dense plasma
open: Validate alpha-energy deposition under the coupled density, temperature, degeneracy, and nonequilibrium conditions of an igniting target.
status: Ignition demonstrates effective self-heating, but it does not uniquely validate every stopping model over the relevant state space.
why: Small stopping differences can shift ignition thresholds and inferred margins.
key_works: Hurricane et al. (2023), *Physics principles of inertial confinement fusion and U.S. program overview*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.95.025005.

title: Equation-of-state and opacity uncertainty
open: Reduce and propagate equation-of-state and opacity uncertainties for fuel, ablators, and mixed material over implosion trajectories.
status: First-principles deuterium and polystyrene tables improved modeling in 2011–2015; complete experimentally constrained coverage remains open.
why: Material-model errors can mimic drive or instability errors.
key_works: Hu et al. (2011), *First-principles equation-of-state table of deuterium for inertial confinement fusion applications*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevB.84.224109; Hu (2015), DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevE.92.043104.

title: Direct-drive ignition
open: Demonstrate actual ignition and useful target gain using direct laser drive, rather than hydrodynamically scaled equivalence.
status: A hydrodynamically equivalent burning-plasma demonstration was published in 2024; that result is not direct-drive ignition itself.
why: Direct drive could offer different efficiency and target-manufacturing tradeoffs.
key_works: Gopalaswamy et al. (2024), *Demonstration of a hydrodynamically equivalent burning plasma in direct-drive inertial confinement fusion*, DOI: 10.1038/s41567-023-02361-4.

title: Shock-ignition coupling
open: Demonstrate that an intense late-time drive can launch the required ignition shock without unacceptable hot-electron preheat or laser–plasma losses.
status: Shock ignition is a studied alternative target scheme; integrated high-gain experimental validation remains open.
why: It may reduce compression-driver requirements if coupling is favorable.
key_works: Craxton et al. (2015), *Direct-drive inertial confinement fusion: A review*, DOI: 10.1063/1.4934714; Tikhonchuk (2020), *Progress and opportunities for inertial fusion energy in Europe*.

title: Fast-ignition energy deposition
open: Deliver a sufficiently concentrated electron or ion energy pulse into compressed fuel with acceptable conversion, transport, and pointing efficiency.
status: Fast ignition has a substantial research literature; integrated target gain remains unresolved.
why: Separating compression from ignition could enlarge target-design options.
key_works: Betti and Hurricane (2016), *Inertial-confinement fusion with lasers*, DOI: 10.1038/nphys3736; Tikhonchuk (2020), *Progress and opportunities for inertial fusion energy in Europe*.

title: Predictive cross-beam energy transfer
open: Predict and control cross-beam energy transfer in evolving, multidimensional target plasmas over the full pulse.
status: Wavelength detuning demonstrated mitigation in 2018; complete predictive control across target designs remains open.
why: Energy redistribution changes implosion symmetry and useful coupling.
key_works: Marozas et al. (2018), *First observation of cross-beam energy transfer mitigation for direct-drive inertial confinement fusion implosions using wavelength detuning at the national ignition facility*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.085001.

title: Two-plasmon-decay hot-electron control
open: Bound and suppress hot-electron generation from two-plasmon decay under ignition-scale direct-drive conditions.
status: The instability and mitigation approaches are longstanding; acceptable reactor-target performance remains configuration-dependent.
why: Premature fuel heating can prevent adequate compression.
key_works: Craxton et al. (2015), *Direct-drive inertial confinement fusion: A review*, DOI: 10.1063/1.4934714.

title: Raman and Brillouin backscatter prediction
open: Predict stimulated scattering and its saturation in realistic speckled, broadband, evolving fusion plasmas.
status: Detailed models exist, but full-scale quantitative prediction remains difficult because multiple kinetic and optical effects interact.
why: Backscatter wastes driver energy and can damage optics.
key_works: Tikhonchuk (2020), *Progress and opportunities for inertial fusion energy in Europe*.

title: Self-generated magnetic fields in laser targets
open: Predict how Biermann generation, thermomagnetic transport, and reconnection alter heat flow and symmetry throughout an implosion.
status: These effects are represented in advanced models; validated integrated impact remains uncertain.
why: Unplanned magnetization can change transport even in nominally unmagnetized targets.
key_works: Hurricane et al. (2023), *Physics principles of inertial confinement fusion and U.S. program overview*, DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.95.025005.

title: Broadband-driver instability suppression
open: Demonstrate that realistic bandwidth and beam-smoothing architectures suppress damaging laser–plasma instabilities without unacceptable efficiency or optical penalties.
status: Broadband and smoothing strategies are active design approaches; integrated high-gain benefits need experimental validation.
why: Driver design and plasma instability control must be optimized together.
key_works: Tikhonchuk (2020), *Progress and opportunities for inertial fusion energy in Europe*; Craxton et al. (2015), DOI: 10.1063/1.4934714.

title: Efficient repetitive megajoule-class laser systems
open: Combine fusion-relevant pulse energy, waveform, wavelength, repetition rate, efficiency, and lifetime in one complete driver.
status: Diode-pumped systems demonstrate important smaller-scale capabilities; IFE workshops identify roughly 10–20% driver efficiency as a development objective, not a completed system.
why: Single-shot high energy and high-repetition low energy are not interchangeable achievements.
key_works: Ma (2023), *Priority Research Opportunities from the 2022 DOE Basic Research Needs for Inertial Fusion Energy*; Gorman et al. (2024), DOI: 10.1063/5.0201702.

title: Long-lived ultraviolet final optics
open: Qualify final optics against cumulative laser damage, contamination, neutrons, debris, thermal distortion, and repair requirements.
status: NIF uses sophisticated optics inspection and maintenance; power-plant repetition changes the lifetime requirement dramatically.
why: Optics replacement can dominate driver availability and operating cost.
key_works: LLNL (2026), *Meet the Machines That Matter: The Optics Inspector*; Ma (2023), IFE research opportunities.

title: Heavy-ion driver compression and focusing
open: Deliver an intense heavy-ion pulse with the required temporal compression and spot size through a realistic fusion chamber.
status: Heavy-ion fusion remains a studied driver alternative; an integrated high-gain driver–target demonstration is not established.
why: Accelerator drivers may offer attractive efficiency and repetition if beam transport can be solved.
key_works: Wurzel and Hsu (2022), *Progress toward fusion energy breakeven and gain as measured against the Lawson criterion*, DOI: 10.1063/5.0083990; NASEM (2021), DOI: 10.17226/25991.

title: Low-cost precision target manufacturing
open: Manufacture ignition-capable targets at industrial throughput with a verified delivered cost compatible with plant economics.
status: The 2023 IFE workshop presentation discusses approximately million-per-day production and sub-dollar targets as objectives; these are not demonstrated production records.
why: A consumable used several times per second cannot retain laboratory-production economics.
key_works: Ma (2023), *Priority Research Opportunities from the 2022 DOE Basic Research Needs for Inertial Fusion Energy*.

title: Inline target qualification
open: Detect all performance-relevant target defects rapidly enough for production, with validated false-accept and false-reject rates.
status: Experimental target metrology is sophisticated; production-speed predictive acceptance remains an unresolved industrial step.
why: Manufacturing throughput is useless if bad targets cannot be identified economically.
