open: Derive and validate an adaptive rule for when to perform mixed-variable pullback transformations, balancing computational cost against noise, conservation error, and physical signal loss.
status: Pullback implementation in ORB5 provides an established algorithmic foundation; a generally reliable adaptive operating rule is a separate optimization problem.
why: An unnecessarily frequent correction wastes computation, while an insufficient correction can corrupt weak electromagnetic signals.
key_works: Mishchenko et al. (2018), *Pullback scheme implementation in ORB5*, arXiv:1811.05346.

title: Electromagnetic verification beyond linear waves
open: Establish nonlinear verification cases with known invariants and independently converged solutions that test electromagnetic gyrokinetic codes beyond linear Alfvén-wave propagation.
status: The 2025 PICLS electromagnetic verification work supplies manufactured and wave-based tests. Nonlinear turbulence and reconnection require additional discriminating tests.
why: Passing a linear test does not establish that nonlinear field–particle energy transfer is correct.
key_works: Stier et al. (2025), *Verification of the PICLS electromagnetic upgrade in mixed variables*, arXiv:2503.17188.

title: Field-aligned discretization at X points
open: Quantify and eliminate numerical transport caused by field-aligned meshes near X points, separatrices, and transitions between closed and open field lines.
status: A 2026 high-order triangular finite-element formulation demonstrates progress on open-field-line geometry; robust error control across changing topology remains a distinct requirement.
why: Artificial cross-field diffusion is especially damaging where the physical transport barrier is narrow.
key_works: Lu et al. (2026), *A High-order piecewise field-aligned triangular finite element method for electromagnetic gyrokinetic particle simulations of tokamak plasmas with open field lines*, arXiv:2602.03759.

title: Collision-operator dependence of nonlinear thresholds
open: Determine which differences in predicted critical gradients and saturated transport are physical consequences of collisions and which are artifacts of collision models or velocity-space dissipation.
status: Gyro-moment Dimits-shift studies explicitly investigate collision and resolution effects. Their results motivate systematic, cross-operator nonlinear convergence tests.
why: A numerically convenient collision model should not determine the apparent operating margin.
key_works: Hoffmann et al. (2023), *Gyrokinetic moment-based simulations of the Dimits shift*, arXiv:2308.01016.

title: Closures that retain stochastic plasma echoes
open: Construct reduced kinetic closures that reproduce both phase mixing and nonlinear anti-phase-mixing rather than treating all fine velocity-space structure as irreversibly damped.
status: Drift-kinetic theory and simulations established the importance of nonlinear echoes in 2015–2016. Compact closures that preserve this competition across fusion regimes remain unresolved.
why: Overdamping velocity-space structure can overestimate heating and underestimate fluctuations.
key_works: Schekochihin et al. (2015 preprint), *Phase mixing vs. nonlinear advection in drift-kinetic plasma turbulence*, arXiv:1508.05988.

title: Experimental measurement of anti-phase-mixing
open: Identify an experimentally measurable signature that separates nonlinear return of free energy from velocity space from ordinary collisional damping or changing drive.
status: Suppression of phase mixing is demonstrated in drift-kinetic calculations; an unambiguous fusion-experiment diagnostic is a separate challenge.
why: It would test whether a major kinetic mechanism operates with the strength assumed in transport models.
key_works: Parker et al. (2016), *Suppression of phase mixing in drift-kinetic plasma turbulence*, arXiv:1603.06968.

title: Electromagnetic survival of echo-mediated cancellation
open: Determine when electromagnetic fluctuations, magnetic stochasticity, and multiple species destroy or preserve the phase-mixing cancellation found in simpler electrostatic systems.
status: Existing drift-kinetic results establish mechanisms in restricted models, not a universal cancellation law for burning-plasma turbulence.
why: The answer controls how confidently simplified kinetic-heating predictions can be extrapolated.
key_works: Schekochihin et al. (2015), *Phase mixing vs. nonlinear advection in drift-kinetic plasma turbulence*, arXiv:1508.05988.

title: Three-dimensional gyrokinetic dissipation anomaly
open: Establish whether driven electromagnetic gyrokinetic turbulence retains finite irreversible entropy production as physical collisionality tends to zero, and specify the required regularity and forcing assumptions.
status: Entropy-cascade theory and reduced gyrokinetic studies provide a foundation; the full three-dimensional electromagnetic statement is stronger.
why: It would clarify how nearly collisionless plasma converts turbulent energy into heat.
key_works: Tatsuno et al. (2008 preprint), *Nonlinear phase mixing and phase-space cascade of entropy in gyrokinetic plasma turbulence*, arXiv:0811.2538.

title: Species-resolved irreversible turbulent heating
open: Separate reversible field–particle energy exchange from true entropy production for each species and predict their ratio under changing turbulence conditions.
status: Phase-space cascades and suppressed phase mixing show why instantaneous energy transfer is not automatically irreversible heating.
why: Ion–electron heating partition affects fusion reactivity, radiation losses, and auxiliary heating requirements.
key_works: Tatsuno et al. (2008), arXiv:0811.2538; Parker et al. (2016), *Suppression of phase mixing in drift-kinetic plasma turbulence*, arXiv:1603.06968.

title: Minimum perturbation for subcritical plasma turbulence
open: Find the smallest physically realizable perturbation that triggers sustained turbulence in a linearly stable, sheared fusion plasma, including its spatial and velocity-space structure.
status: Subcritical transition has been investigated in tokamak-relevant gyrokinetic calculations since at least 2016; a general minimal-seed characterization remains open.
why: Linear stability may substantially overstate resilience to pellets, edge events, or actuator disturbances.
key_works: van Wyk et al. (2016), *Transition to subcritical turbulence in a tokamak plasma*, arXiv:1607.08173.

title: Turbulent lifetime distributions near threshold
open: Determine whether near-threshold plasma turbulence decays, persists indefinitely, or exhibits system-size-dependent metastability, and measure the corresponding lifetime distributions.
status: MAST-oriented studies connect subcritical simulations to measurements; distinguishing long transients from genuinely sustained states remains essential.
why: A discharge lasting less than a turbulent lifetime can misidentify the underlying stability boundary.
key_works: van Wyk et al. (2017), *Ion-scale turbulence in MAST: anomalous transport, subcritical transitions, and comparison to BES measurements*, arXiv:1704.02830.

title: Kinetic extension of the zero-turbulence manifold
open: Determine how the boundary separating turbulent and nonturbulent states changes with kinetic electrons, finite beta, impurities, and realistic momentum constraints.
status: A zero-turbulence manifold was mapped in a restricted toroidal model in 2012. Its existence there does not establish the reactor-relevant manifold.
why: This could identify genuinely accessible low-transport operating regions.
key_works: Highcock et al. (2012), *Zero-Turbulence Manifold in a Toroidal Plasma*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.109.265001.

title: Useful nonlinear stability certificates
open: Convert gyrokinetic free-energy inequalities into computable certificates that rule out sustained turbulence over practically useful regions of parameter space.
status: Rigorous energetic bounds already exist; making them sufficiently sharp to guide operating decisions is the unresolved step.
why: A certificate could establish safety margins without exhaustively simulating every perturbation.
key_works: Helander and Plunk (2021), *Upper bounds on gyrokinetic instabilities*, arXiv:2108.12455.

title: Sharp stationary gyrokinetic heat-flux bounds
open: Obtain geometry-sensitive, asymptotically sharp bounds on statistically stationary heat transport, or prove why a specified class of bounds cannot be sharp.
status: Bounds on instability and free-energy growth are established. The requested result is a stronger transport bound with demonstrated usefulness, not merely another finite inequality.
why: Sharp bounds could expose intrinsic confinement limits and constrain optimization claims.
key_works: Helander and Plunk (2021), *Energetic bounds on gyrokinetic instabilities. Part I: Fundamentals*, arXiv:2112.09504.

title: Staircase step-size selection
open: Predict the spacing and amplitude of self-organized transport staircases from plasma parameters, including why adjacent steps merge or remain separated.
status: Cross-phase models and simulations explain mechanisms for staircase formation; a universal quantitative selection law is not established.
why: Barrier spacing influences global profile shape and intermittent transport.
key_works: Leconte and Kobayashi (2021), *Zonal profile corrugations and staircase formation: Role of the transport crossphase*, arXiv:2111.06022.

title: Staircase survival under reactor scaling
open: Determine whether transport staircases survive decreasing normalized gyroradius, evolving profiles, electromagnetic turbulence, and realistic sources, rather than being finite-domain structures.
status: Global simulations established staircase phenomenology; reactor-scale persistence is a separate extrapolation problem.
why: A confinement mechanism that disappears with size cannot justify reactor design assumptions.
key_works: Dif-Pradalier et al. (2017), *The E×B staircase of magnetised plasmas*.

title: Correct isotope scaling of molecular charge exchange
open: Replace simple hydrogen-to-deuterium/tritium mass rescaling with validated, state-resolved molecular charge-exchange rates for the isotopic mixtures used in reactors.
status: A 2023 SOLPS-ITER investigation showed that default rescaling could underestimate molecular-ion production and materially change predicted detachment behavior.
why: Incorrect rates can produce the wrong recombination, radiation, and target-current predictions.
key_works: Verhaegh et al. (2023), *Investigating the impact of the molecular charge-exchange rate on detached SOLPS-ITER simulations*, DOI: 10.1088/1741-4326/acd394; arXiv:2301.11298.

title: Vibrationally resolved charge-exchange uncertainty
open: Establish uncertainty distributions and correlations for charge-exchange cross-sections by vibrational state, and propagate them into detached-plasma predictions.
status: The 2023 analysis identifies differences among underlying cross-section calculations as well as problems with effective-rate construction.
why: A single effective rate can hide the state populations responsible for the largest uncertainty.
key_works: Verhaegh et al. (2023), *Investigating the impact of the molecular charge-exchange rate on detached SOLPS-ITER simulations*, DOI: 10.1088/1741-4326/acd394.

title: Non-Boltzmann rovibrational population transport
open: Predict molecular rovibrational populations using transport, wall formation, excitation, and destruction, rather than assigning one rotational and one vibrational temperature everywhere.
status: LHD measurements and collisional-radiative comparisons establish parameter-dependent populations; a two-temperature description does not uniquely determine the full distribution.
why: High vibrational states can disproportionately control molecular reaction pathways.
key_works: Fujii et al. (2023), *Plasma-Parameter Dependence of Ro-Vibrational Temperatures for H₂ in LHD Divertor*, arXiv:2302.08587.

title: Wall-memory effects on molecular excitation
open: Determine how wall temperature, implanted isotopes, surface composition, and prior exposure change the internal-state distribution of molecules entering the divertor.
status: Spectroscopic population measurements provide constraints, but reconstructing the wall-dependent source distribution remains a separate inverse problem.
why: Identical upstream plasma settings may produce different detachment behavior after wall conditioning.
key_works: Fujii et al. (2023), *Plasma-Parameter Dependence of Ro-Vibrational Temperatures for H₂ in LHD Divertor*, arXiv:2302.08587.

title: Molecular momentum-loss closure
open: Infer and predict the spatial distribution of momentum transfer from plasma to molecules, including repeated collisions during long molecular residence times.
status: MAST-U and TCV analyses associate molecular heating with substantial momentum losses; the inference still uses reduced descriptions.
why: Momentum removal is central to detachment and cannot be inferred from radiation alone.
key_works: Osborne et al. (2024–2025), *A novel understanding of the role of plasma-molecular kinetics on divertor power exhaust*, arXiv:2410.14403.

title: Spectroscopically hidden cold molecular populations
open: Quantify molecules that contribute to transport and chemistry but are poorly represented by the observed emission bands, and correct diagnostic weighting accordingly.
status: Recent molecular-kinetics studies compare inferred distributions with collisional-radiative predictions and report remaining disagreements.
why: Emission-weighted temperatures need not represent the molecules carrying most mass or momentum.
key_works: Osborne et al. (2024–2025), *A novel understanding of the role of plasma-molecular kinetics on divertor power exhaust*, arXiv:2410.14403.

title: Negative-ion contribution to molecular-assisted recombination
open: Separate and quantify recombination mediated by negative hydrogen isotopes from pathways involving positive molecular ions under strongly detached conditions.
status: MAST-U studies identify molecular channels and possible negative-ion contributions; their relative importance requires stronger experimental discrimination.
why: Different pathways respond differently to isotope composition, vibrational excitation, and electron temperature.
key_works: Verhaegh et al. (2023), *Investigations of atomic & molecular processes of NBI-heated discharges in the MAST Upgrade Super-X divertor with implications for reactors*, arXiv:2311.08580.

title: Molecular-assisted dissociation power accounting
open: Close the power balance for molecular-assisted dissociation, including fragment kinetic energy, subsequent ionization, radiation, and energy ultimately deposited on surfaces.
status: MAST-U analyses infer consequential dissociation-related power sinks; a reaction’s local energy removal is not necessarily its net plant-facing exhaust benefit.
why: Misallocated chemical energy can create apparent unexplained divertor power.
key_works: Verhaegh et al. (2023), *Investigations of atomic & molecular processes of NBI-heated discharges in the MAST Upgrade Super-X divertor with implications for reactors*, arXiv:2311.08580.

title: Sub-electronvolt ion–molecule elastic collisions
open: Validate momentum and energy-transfer operators for ion–molecule elastic collisions in the very cold regions of detached divertors.
status: Dedicated SOLPS-ITER predictions published in 2023 examine these collisions in strongly detached MAST-U conditions; direct discriminating validation remains needed.
why: Processes negligible in hotter plasma can control pressure balance below approximately one electronvolt.
key_works: Myatra et al. (2023), *SOLPS-ITER predictive simulations of the impact of ion-molecule elastic collisions on strongly detached MAST-U Super-X divertor conditions*, *Nuclear Fusion* 63, 076030.

title: Self-consistent Lyman-opacity feedback
open: Couple line trapping to level populations, ionization, recombination, and energy transport, and validate the resulting detached-plasma solution rather than applying an opacity correction afterward.
status: Lyman-opacity calculations for high-recycling and detached divertors were published in 2024; diagnostic correction and full dynamical coupling are different tasks.
why: Trapped photons can alter the plasma state whose radiation is being interpreted.
key_works: Chandra et al. (2024), *Lyman line opacities in tokamak divertor plasmas under high-recycling and detached conditions*, DOI: 10.1016/j.nme.2024.101794.

title: Sheath structure below the critical grazing angle
open: Determine the physically selected sheath configuration below the angle at which monotonic solutions cease to exist, allowing kinetic electrons and finite Debye length.
status: A 2025 study characterizes monotonic grazing-incidence sheaths and their critical-angle boundary; the boundary is not a complete description of the state below it.
why: Reactor divertors deliberately use shallow incidence to spread heat.
key_works: Geraldini et al. (2025), *Characteristics of monotonic sheaths near a wall with grazing magnetic incidence*, arXiv:2508.09067.

title: Dynamic crossing of the sheath critical angle
open: Predict whether changes in field angle or plasma conditions produce smooth transitions, hysteresis, oscillations, or abrupt changes in wall loading near the critical-angle boundary.
status: Stationary monotonic-sheath calculations constrain possible equilibria; transient selection and stability require additional analysis.
why: Small geometry or plasma changes should not cause unanticipated jumps in surface exposure.
key_works: Geraldini et al. (2025), *Characteristics of monotonic sheaths near a wall with grazing magnetic incidence*, arXiv:2508.09067.

title: Ion-impact distributions outside the large-orbit limit
open: Develop fast, validated ion energy–angle distributions at the wall when ion temperature, incidence angle, or electron response lies outside the simplifying limits of analytic large-orbit models.
status: Geraldini’s model supplies a useful approximation under explicit temperature and scale-separation assumptions.
why: Sputtering calculations require distributions, not just mean impact energy.
key_works: Geraldini (2021), *Large gyro-orbit model of ion velocity distribution in plasma near a wall in a grazing-angle magnetic field*, DOI: 10.1017/S002237782000166X; arXiv:2007.05806.

title: Transient ion orbits during edge bursts
open: Determine how rapidly changing electric fields modify ion-impact distributions when a transient evolves on times comparable to presheath transit or gyro-motion.
status: Stationary orbit models establish the baseline; applying their instantaneous solutions to fast transients is an additional approximation requiring validation.
why: Transient erosion can depend on brief high-energy or unfavorable-angle populations.
key_works: Geraldini (2021), *Large gyro-orbit model of ion velocity distribution in plasma near a wall in a grazing-angle magnetic field*, arXiv:2007.05806.

title: Rough-surface gyro-orbit interception
open: Predict first-impact locations and energy–angle distributions on surfaces whose roughness and feature size are comparable to relevant gyroradii.
status: Grazing-angle gyrokinetic theories describe idealized geometry. Replacing actual topography by a single roughness parameter need not preserve orbit interception.
why: Surface evolution can invalidate erosion estimates made for a smooth target.
key_works: Geraldini, Parra, and Militello (2016), *Gyrokinetic treatment of a grazing angle magnetic field*, arXiv:1608.02002.

title: Collisional magnetic presheaths in detached plasma
open: Connect the grazing-angle magnetic presheath to charge exchange and ion–molecule collisions when the mean free path is no longer well separated from orbit scales.
status: Collisionless and ordered presheath theories provide limiting cases; cold detached conditions demand a controlled collisional extension.
why: The ion distribution arriving at the wall may differ substantially from a collisionless prediction.
key_works: Geraldini et al. (2016), arXiv:1608.02002; Myatra et al. (2023), *Nuclear Fusion* 63, 076030.

title: Secondary-emission sheath transitions on reactor surfaces
open: Establish when irradiated, contaminated, or evolving plasma-facing surfaces enter emission-dominated sheath states and determine their consequences for electron heat flux.
status: The absence of a conventional Debye sheath under strong secondary emission was demonstrated theoretically in 2012; reactor-surface transition maps remain a separate problem.
why: Surface emission can invalidate standard wall-potential and heat-transmission assumptions.
key_works: Campanell, Khrabrov, and Kaganovich (2012), *Absence of Debye Sheaths due to Secondary Electron Emission*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.108.255001.

title: Thermionic emission coupled to surface overheating
open: Determine whether strong thermionic emission stabilizes or amplifies overheating of plasma-facing surfaces when sheath potential, electron return current, and material temperature evolve together.
status: Strongly emitting surfaces need not float below plasma potential; translating this result into a predictive thermal-feedback model remains open.
why: Emission changes the heat balance precisely when a surface approaches damage.
key_works: Campanell and Umansky (2016), *Strongly Emitting Surfaces Unable to Float below Plasma Potential*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.116.085003.

title: Consequences of the unfavorable maximum-J minority
open: Determine whether the small population of particles violating maximum-J behavior in optimized vacuum quasi-isodynamic fields can drive consequential instabilities or losses.
status: A published construction gives favorable behavior for 99.6% of trapped particles while identifying an unavoidable unfavorable shallowly trapped population.
why: A small phase-space fraction can matter disproportionately if it resonates strongly.
key_works: Rodríguez, Helander, and Goodman (2023 preprint), *The maximum-J property in quasi-isodynamic stellarators*, arXiv:2311.14439.

title: Maximum-J preservation during pressure evolution
open: Design and validate operating trajectories that preserve favorable trapped-particle precession as pressure, bootstrap current, and profiles evolve from startup to full performance.
status: Vacuum and finite-pressure constructions establish favorable configurations; they do not automatically establish a connected, robust operating path.
why: A desirable endpoint may be inaccessible without crossing a strongly unstable intermediate state.
key_works: Rodríguez, Helander, and Goodman (2023), *The maximum-J property in quasi-isodynamic stellarators*, arXiv:2311.14439.

title: Electromagnetic limits of maximum-J turbulence suppression
open: Determine which suppression mechanisms survive finite-beta electromagnetic fluctuations, collisions, and multiple kinetic species.
status: Maximum-J studies demonstrate suppression or mitigation of important electrostatic instabilities; this is not a theorem covering all reactor turbulence.
why: Optimizing away trapped-electron drive may expose a different dominant instability.
key_works: Alcusón et al. (2020), *Suppression of electrostatic micro-instabilities in maximum-J stellarators*; Proll et al. (2022), *Turbulence mitigation in maximum-J stellarators with electron-density gradient*, DOI: 10.1017/S002237782200006X.

title: Available-energy proxies outside their training configurations
open: Establish when trapped-electron available energy reliably ranks nonlinear turbulent transport across geometries, gradients, collisions, and electromagnetic regimes.
status: A 2022 study demonstrated useful relationships; a 2023 erratum must be incorporated when reproducing the result.
why: A cheap optimization proxy is valuable only where its ranking remains reliable.
key_works: Mackenbach, Proll, and Helander (2022), *Available Energy of Trapped Electrons and Its Relation to Turbulent Transport*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.128.175001; erratum DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.130.239901.

title: Uniform treatment of merging neoclassical regimes
open: Extend asymptotic descriptions of merging superbanana-plateau and square-root-collisionality regimes to realistic profiles, multiple species, and departures from near-quasisymmetry.
status: Catto, Tolman, and Parra derived a merged treatment for nearly quasisymmetric stellarators in 2023; the restricted result should not be mistaken for a universal closure.
why: Regime boundaries can occur inside the operating window of an optimized reactor.
key_works: Catto et al. (2023), *Merging of the superbanana plateau and √ν transport regimes in nearly quasisymmetric stellarators*, DOI: 10.1017/S0022377822001301.

title: Radially nonlocal transport below the near-omnigenous limit
open: Construct predictive neoclassical transport when collisionality falls below the validity range of radially local near-omnigenous theory.
status: The 2017 tangential-drift analysis explicitly identifies a lower-collisionality breakdown of its formulation.
why: The best-confined, hottest plasmas can approach precisely this difficult regime.
key_works: Calvo et al. (2017), *The effect of tangential drifts on neoclassical transport in stellarators close to omnigeneity*, DOI: 10.1088/1361-6587/aa63ce; arXiv:1610.06016.

title: Full flux-surface electrostatic-potential maps
open: Measure the three-dimensional electrostatic variation on a flux surface accurately enough to discriminate competing impurity-transport models.
status: TJ-II measurements reported substantial potential variations and partial agreement with calculations; local discrepancies remained.
why: Small potential variations relative to bulk temperature can strongly affect high-charge impurities.
key_works: Pedrosa et al. (2015), *Electrostatic potential variations along flux surfaces in stellarators*, DOI: 10.1088/0029-5515/55/5/052001; arXiv:1404.0932.

title: Electric-root transition fronts
open: Predict the position, propagation, and stability of transitions between ambipolar electric-field roots, including finite orbit widths and profile feedback.
status: Neoclassical theory identifies strong radial-electric-field dependence; selecting a spatially evolving root is more demanding than solving a local ambipolarity equation.
why: Root transitions can reorganize confinement and impurity transport.
key_works: Calvo et al. (2017), *The effect of tangential drifts on neoclassical transport in stellarators close to omnigeneity*, arXiv:1610.06016.

title: Nonlinear significance of stellarator zonal-flow oscillations
open: Determine when the observed oscillatory relaxation of radial electric fields materially changes sustained turbulence rather than merely describing a linear relaxation experiment.
status: Oscillatory relaxation was observed experimentally in 2017, and semianalytical frequency calculations exist.
why: A measurable mode is useful for design only if its nonlinear confinement role is understood.
key_works: Alonso et al. (2017), *Observation of Oscillatory Radial Electric Field Relaxation in a Stellarator Plasma*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.118.185002; Monreal et al. (2017), arXiv:1701.02722.

title: Impurity modification of zonal-flow relaxation
open: Predict how realistic impurity mixtures change zonal-flow frequency, damping, residual flow, and resulting turbulent transport.
status: Multispecies relaxation calculations were published in 2018; demonstrating the resulting confinement impact across impurity regimes remains open.
why: Impurities may alter transport indirectly through the flows that regulate turbulence.
key_works: Sánchez et al. (2018), *Oscillatory relaxation of zonal flows in a multi-species stellarator plasma*, arXiv:1801.09495.

title: Physical regularization of Pfirsch–Schlüter singularities
open: Determine how finite resistivity, kinetic effects, pressure flattening, and magnetic islands regularize resonant pressure-driven currents in realistic three-dimensional equilibria.
status: Quasisymmetric current-singularity analysis identifies favorable leading-order structure but does not eliminate all higher-order resonances.
why: Idealized smooth equilibria may conceal localized current layers affecting stability and transport.
key_works: Rodríguez and Bhattacharjee (2021), *Islands and current singularities in quasisymmetric toroidal plasmas*, DOI: 10.1063/5.0057186; arXiv:2105.07807.

title: Higher-order island formation in precise quasisymmetry
open: Quantify island widths and confinement consequences arising from higher-order departures that remain after leading quasisymmetry-related resonances are controlled.
status: The 2021 analysis distinguishes leading-order simplifications from unresolved higher-order island structure.
why: Extremely small symmetry errors are not automatically harmless near resonances.
key_works: Rodríguez and Bhattacharjee (2021), *Islands and current singularities in quasisymmetric toroidal plasmas*, DOI: 10.1063/5.0057186.

title: Self-consistent pressure flattening near stellarator islands
open: Determine island pressure profiles and associated currents from coupled transport and equilibrium, rather than prescribing flattening independently.
status: Pressure-driven currents near islands were analyzed in 2016; self-consistent profile selection remains a further coupled problem.
why: Assumed pressure flattening changes both predicted island structure and stability.
key_works: Reiman et al. (2016), *Pressure driven currents near magnetic islands in 3D MHD equilibria*, *Physics of Plasmas* 23, 072502.

title: Dynamically accessible island elimination
open: Establish when boundary adjustments that eliminate islands in equilibrium calculations can actually produce the desired state through finite-resistivity plasma evolution.
status: High-pressure free-boundary equilibrium optimization demonstrated island elimination in 2002; equilibrium existence does not establish dynamical accessibility.
why: A numerically optimized topology may not be the state reached by an experiment.
key_works: Hudson et al. (2002), *Eliminating Islands in High-Pressure Free-Boundary Stellarator Magnetohydrodynamic Equilibrium Solutions*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.89.275003.

title: Correlated-error stellarator coil optimization
open: Optimize against measured distributions of correlated manufacturing, assembly, and deformation errors rather than convenient independent perturbations.
status: Stochastic and conventional coil optimizations have been compared physically; reliable error-distribution selection remains consequential.
why: Robustness to the wrong error model may provide little protection in the assembled machine.
key_works: Lobsien et al. (2020), *Physics analysis of results of stochastic and classic stellarator coil optimization*, DOI: 10.1088/1741-4326/ab7211.

title: Certified relaxation gaps in coil optimization
open: Bound the difference between an optimized continuous-current representation and the best manufacturable discrete-coil realization, including cases where a global optimum is not certified.
status: QUADCOIL provides exact global solutions in some parameter regions and useful approximate solutions elsewhere; extracting certified physical-coil quality remains a distinct problem.
why: A favorable mathematical relaxation may conceal expensive discretization losses.
key_works: Fu et al. (2024–2025), *Global Stellarator Coil Optimization with Quadratic Constraints and Objectives*, arXiv:2408.08267.

title: Quantified flexibility of optimized stellarators
open: Optimize not just one plasma configuration but a sufficiently broad family reachable with permitted coil currents, while maintaining conductor-strain and engineering constraints.
status: CSX single-stage design incorporates engineering constraints and possible auxiliary coils; a general quantitative flexibility–performance tradeoff remains open.
why: An exceptionally optimized but inflexible machine may be difficult to commission or operate.
key_works: Baillod et al. (2024), *Integrating Novel Stellarator Single-Stage Optimization Algorithms to Design the Columbia Stellarator Experiment*, arXiv:2409.05261.

title: Permanent-magnet field drift under reactor exposure
open: Qualify permanent-magnet stellarator architectures against temperature history, irradiation, demagnetization, and spatially nonuniform aging.
status: Permanent-magnet stellarator fields are a demonstrated design concept; reactor-exposure field stability is an additional qualification problem.
why: Small irreversible field changes can accumulate into unacceptable confinement errors.
key_works: Helander et al. (2020), *Stellarators with Permanent Magnets*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.124.095001.

title: Experimental discrimination of hydrogen self-clustering
open: Distinguish hydrogen self-clustering in tungsten from trapping at pre-existing vacancies, dislocations, or impurities using experiments with independently characterized defect populations.
status: Density-functional and statistical models predict self-clustering mechanisms; their quantitative contribution under plasma exposure remains to be isolated.
why: Different nucleation mechanisms imply different retention and blister-prevention strategies.
key_works: Hou et al. (2017), *Hydrogen bubble nucleation by self-clustering: Density Functional Theory and statistical models studies using tungsten as a model system*, arXiv:1712.09606.

title: Hydrogen-cluster-to-blister transition
open: Connect atomic-scale hydrogen clusters to experimentally measurable platelet growth, bubble pressure, fracture, and surface blistering under time-dependent implantation.
status: Atomistic cluster predictions do not yet supply a complete multiscale blister-onset law.
why: Surface damage can begin well before a bulk-average retention limit appears problematic.
key_works: Hou et al. (2017), *Hydrogen bubble nucleation by self-clustering*, arXiv:1712.09606.

title: High-dose tungsten-fiber composite toughness
open: Establish whether tungsten-fiber-reinforced tungsten retains useful fracture resistance at substantially higher fusion-relevant exposure than the first neutron campaigns, with thermal cycling included.
status: A 2026 study reports approximately 0.7–0.8 dpa tests at 600°C and 1,000°C. This is important neutron evidence, not lifetime qualification.
why: Composite toughening could fail through irradiation mechanisms absent from unirradiated tests.
key_works: Riesch et al. (2026), *Effect of neutron irradiation on the fracture behaviour of tungsten fibre-reinforced tungsten composites*, DOI: 10.1016/j.jnucmat.2026.156601.

title: Irradiation-stable fiber debonding window
open: Preserve the interface-strength range that permits crack deflection and fiber pullout without premature loss of structural integrity.
status: The 2026 neutron study finds different responses for long-fiber and short-fiber composite routes, emphasizing architecture and interface dependence.
why: Toughness depends on controlled interface failure, not simply maximizing bond strength.
key_works: Riesch et al. (2026), *Effect of neutron irradiation on the fracture behaviour of tungsten fibre-reinforced tungsten composites*, DOI: 10.1016/j.jnucmat.2026.156601.

title: Self-passivation after preferential alloy erosion
open: Determine whether W–Cr–Y and related self-passivating alloys retain protective oxidation behavior after plasma exposure preferentially removes alloying elements.
status: Self-passivating tungsten alloys have demonstrated favorable oxidation behavior; the surface composition after service is a separate qualification variable.
why: Accident protection must work on the used component, not just a freshly manufactured specimen.
key_works: Calvo et al. (2018), *Self-passivating tungsten alloys of the system W-Cr-Y for high temperature applications*, DOI: 10.1016/j.ijrmhm.2018.01.018.

title: Stability of protective oxide phase assemblages
open: Determine which oxide phases form, transform, crack, or volatilize across realistic temperature and oxygen-potential histories of self-passivating tungsten alloys.
status: A 2025 study specifically investigates oxide-phase stability in W–Cr–Y SMART alloys; service-history and irradiation coupling remain additional questions.
why: Protection depends on the actual phase assemblage, not simply the presence of an oxide.
key_works: Kerr et al. (2025), *Stability of oxide phases in W–Cr–Y SMART alloys*.

title: Crack-tolerant tungsten accident passivation
open: Establish whether protective scales reform rapidly enough on repeatedly cracked or thermally shocked tungsten alloys to limit release during an oxidizing accident.
status: Oxidation-resistant alloy reviews document substantial progress, but intact-coupon oxidation performance does not settle cracked-component behavior.
why: The accident most requiring protection may also damage the protective layer.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2021), *Oxidation protection of tungsten alloys for nuclear fusion applications: A comprehensive review*, DOI: 10.1016/j.jallcom.2021.161057.

title: Helium-defect structure versus thermal conductivity
open: Determine which helium-induced defect populations dominate tungsten thermal-conductivity degradation and whether their signatures can be measured nondestructively.
status: Helium-implantation research links microstructure to properties, but translating mixed defect populations into component heat-transfer predictions remains incomplete.
why: Local conductivity loss can amplify temperature and damage without a visible macroscopic crack.
key_works: Hofmann et al. (2017), *Helium-Ion-Implantation in Tungsten: Progress towards a Coherent Understanding of the Damage Formed and its Effects on Properties*.

title: Statistical dust adhesion on used surfaces
open: Measure the distribution—not only the average—of adhesion forces for reactor-relevant dust on rough, contaminated, thermally cycled surfaces.
status: Tungsten-dust remobilization experiments establish strong dependence on contact and exposure conditions; predictive population-level adhesion remains difficult.
why: The weakly attached tail may determine release during a disturbance.
key_works: Ratynskaia et al. (2017), *Tungsten dust remobilization under steady-state and transient plasma conditions*, DOI: 10.1016/j.nme.2016.10.021.

title: Rolling, sliding, and lift-off competition for dust
open: Predict which remobilization pathway dominates under transient plasma forces and thermal loading, including contact modification during the event.
status: Steady-state and transient experiments provide evidence beyond simple force-balance models; transferring that evidence to evolving reactor dust remains unresolved.
why: A lift-off-only model can miss particles that first roll or slide into a vulnerable position.
key_works: Ratynskaia et al. (2017), *Tungsten dust remobilization under steady-state and transient plasma conditions*, DOI: 10.1016/j.nme.2016.10.021.

title: CuCrZr precipitate evolution at fusion dose rates
open: Predict competition between ballistic precipitate dissolution and radiation-assisted reprecipitation at fusion-relevant dose rates and temperature histories.
status: A July 2026 study reports strong temperature-dependent irradiation effects and explicitly raises extrapolation challenges; ion-irradiation behavior is not automatically neutron-service behavior.
why: The strengthening mechanism of a leading heat-sink alloy can evolve during operation.
key_works: Barzic et al. (2026), *CuCrZr heat-sink irradiation performance reveals new challenges for thermonuclear fusion reactors*, arXiv:2607.17594.

title: Transmutation-driven CuCrZr phase changes
open: Validate how neutron-generated composition changes alter precipitates, phase stability, conductivity, and strength in CuCrZr over its intended lifetime.
status: The 2026 study combines irradiation observations with transmutation-based projections; the projected long-term phase changes require experimental qualification.
why: An alloy optimized at manufacture may evolve into a different material in service.
key_works: Barzic et al. (2026), *CuCrZr heat-sink irradiation performance reveals new challenges for thermonuclear fusion reactors*, arXiv:2607.17594.

title: Irradiated copper-alloy fracture under realistic constraints
open: Transfer irradiated copper-alloy toughness measurements to thin ligaments, multiaxial thermal stress, and bonded heat-sink geometries without unjustified specimen-scale assumptions.
status: Copper-alloy fracture-toughness measurements date back decades; component geometry and irradiation history complicate direct transfer.
why: A heat sink can fail by fracture even when average stress remains below a nominal strength limit.
key_works: Alexander, Zinkle, and Rowcliffe (1999), *Fracture toughness of copper-base alloys for fusion energy applications*, DOI: 10.1016/S0022-3115(98)00798-3.

title: Heat-treatment sequence after heat-sink joining
open: Find manufacturing sequences that simultaneously preserve copper-alloy strength, conductivity, joint integrity, and irradiation tolerance after all brazing and thermal-processing steps.
status: Copper-alloy applicability studies identify narrow and competing operating constraints; favorable properties before joining do not establish final-component performance.
why: The last manufacturing operation can undo the microstructure created by earlier processing.
key_works: Zinkle (2016), *Applicability of copper alloys for DEMO high heat flux components*, *Physica Scripta* T167, 014004.

title: Interatomic potentials for transmuting materials
open: Develop validated interatomic models that remain reliable as irradiation introduces new elements, gas atoms, defects, and nonequilibrium local chemistry.
status: The 2026 fusion-materials modeling assessment identifies transmutation, chemical complexity, and interatomic-potential development as continuing gaps.
why: A potential accurate for the original alloy may fail on the configurations determining irradiated lifetime.
key_works: Reali et al. (2026), *State of the art, gaps, and prospects in fusion materials theory and modelling*, DOI: 10.1016/j.jnucmat.2026.156512.

title: High-dose microstructure without artificial reinitialization
open: Simulate overlapping cascades and long-time defect evolution while retaining accumulated structural memory across the handoffs between atomistic and mesoscale models.
status: High-dose microstructures and multiscale structural assessment remain explicit themes of the 2026 modeling-gap assessment.
why: Resetting or simplifying the microstructure between scales can erase the mechanisms responsible for saturation or failure.
key_works: Reali et al. (2026), *State of the art, gaps, and prospects in fusion materials theory and modelling*, DOI: 10.1016/j.jnucmat.2026.156512.

title: Differential swelling within SiC composites
open: Predict stresses generated by different swelling and creep responses of fibers, matrix, coatings, and joints under nonuniform irradiation.
status: SiC composite irradiation research establishes favorable attributes and important property changes; constituent-level mismatch remains a component-design issue.
why: Low average swelling does not prevent destructive internal stress.
key_works: Katoh et al. (2007), *Assessment of Silicon Carbide Composites for Advanced Salt-Cooled Reactors*; Knaster et al. (2016), *Materials research for fusion*, DOI: 10.1038/nphys3735.

title: SiC microcrack connectivity and hermeticity
open: Determine when distributed irradiation and thermal microcracks become connected permeation pathways, and establish inspection signals that predict this transition.
status: Composite mechanical integrity and gas-tightness are distinct requirements; favorable strength measurements do not prove sustained hermeticity.
why: A component can remain load-bearing while losing its confinement or coolant-separation function.
key_works: Katoh et al. (2007), *Assessment of Silicon Carbide Composites for Advanced Salt-Cooled Reactors*.

title: Long-term stability of nanoscale defect sinks
open: Determine whether oxide particles and engineered interfaces retain their defect-absorption function after cascade overlap, solute redistribution, and helium accumulation.
status: Sink engineering is an established radiation-resistance strategy; sink survival and changing effectiveness over long exposure remain crucial.
why: Radiation resistance can decay if the microstructure providing it is itself unstable.
key_works: Zinkle and Snead (2014), *Designing Radiation Resistance in Materials for Fusion Energy*, DOI: 10.1146/annurev-matsci-070813-113627.

title: Defect-sink benefits versus helium localization
open: Optimize interfaces that remove damaging point defects without concentrating helium into mechanically dangerous bubbles or weak boundary layers.
status: Radiation-resistant design already exploits interfaces; their beneficial and harmful roles must be balanced rather than assuming more sink area is always better.
why: A strategy that reduces hardening may simultaneously worsen boundary fracture.
key_works: Zinkle and Snead (2014), *Designing Radiation Resistance in Materials for Fusion Energy*, DOI: 10.1146/annurev-matsci-070813-113627.

title: Reactor-useful off-axis helicon current drive
open: Demonstrate controllable off-axis helicon current deposition at useful efficiency under reactor-like profiles, rather than only centrally peaked deposition.
status: September 2026 DIII-D results report the first experimental evidence of helicon current drive, with core deposition and associated current-profile changes. First observation is therefore no longer the open problem.
why: Steady-state tokamaks often need current in specific off-axis regions.
key_works: Lestz et al. (2026), *First Experimental Evidence of Helicon Current Drive*, arXiv:2609.12474; DOI: 10.1103/mbn4-fd4v.

title: Helicon accessibility under edge uncertainty
open: Determine how launcher spectrum and edge-density variation affect core accessibility, parasitic absorption, and current-drive efficiency.
status: Reactor-oriented parameter studies and the 2026 demonstration establish promising regimes; robustness to uncertain edge conditions remains a separate requirement.
why: A theoretically efficient wave is ineffective if operating fluctuations prevent it from reaching the intended region.
key_works: Wu et al. (2023), *Parametric study of helicon wave current drive in CFETR*, arXiv:2306.02580; Lestz et al. (2026), arXiv:2609.12474.

title: Transferable lower-hybrid spectral broadening
open: Predict lower-hybrid spectral evolution from measured edge turbulence without device-specific broadening parameters.
status: Multiscale calculations published in 2022 connect turbulence-induced broadening to lower-hybrid current drive; transfer across machines and regimes remains the discriminator.
why: The launched spectrum is not necessarily the spectrum that drives current.
key_works: Biswas et al. (2022), *Spectral broadening from turbulence in multiscale lower hybrid current drive simulations*, arXiv:2210.02344.

title: Rare-filament control of lower-hybrid losses
open: Determine whether rare, large edge structures dominate lower-hybrid scattering and deposition changes beyond predictions based on average fluctuation spectra.
status: Turbulence-aware current-drive modeling establishes the coupling; adequately sampling intermittent structures is an additional statistical problem.
why: Mean-spectrum agreement can conceal large shot-to-shot or within-shot failures.
key_works: Biswas et al. (2022), *Spectral broadening from turbulence in multiscale lower hybrid current drive simulations*, arXiv:2210.02344.

title: Direct validation of RF current condensation
open: Measure the predicted nonlinear localization of radio-frequency heating and current within a magnetic island, separating it from ordinary deposition changes.
status: RF current condensation was proposed in 2018, with later work developing validation strategies. The mechanism requires a discriminating experimental test.
why: It could reduce the power required to suppress dangerous tearing modes.
key_works: Reiman and Fisch (2018), *Suppression of Tearing Modes by Radio Frequency Current Condensation*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.121.225001; arXiv:1806.09260.

title: Turbulent stiffness versus RF condensation
open: Determine when enhanced turbulent heat transport prevents condensation, shifts its threshold, or creates multiple operating branches.
status: A 2020 model explicitly includes turbulence-enhanced transport; reactor-island validation and transferable closures remain open.
why: Positive heating feedback competes with temperature-gradient-driven losses.
key_works: Rodríguez, Reiman, and Fisch (2020), *RF current condensation in the presence of turbulent enhanced transport*, arXiv:2001.09044.

title: RF shadowing during nonlinear island heating
open: Predict when increased absorption before the island center deprives the desired region of power, and design spectra or launch trajectories that avoid this shadowing.
status: Condensation models identify a competition between beneficial localization and premature absorption.
why: Stronger absorption can paradoxically make stabilization less effective.
key_works: Rodríguez, Reiman, and Fisch (2020), *RF current condensation in the presence of turbulent enhanced transport*, arXiv:2001.09044.

title: Pulsed RF stabilization with equal energy budgets
open: Determine whether pulsed or modulated RF can exploit condensation and island thermal memory to outperform steady injection at equal delivered energy and actuator limits.
status: Condensation-based disruption-avoidance studies provide the physical basis; equal-budget, experimentally validated waveform optimization remains a separate question.
why: Better timing may reduce hardware power without reducing stabilization effectiveness.
key_works: Reiman et al. (2021), *Disruption avoidance via radio frequency current condensation in magnetic islands produced by off-normal events*, *Physics of Plasmas* 28, 042508.

title: Robust O–X–B conversion in turbulent edges
open: Maintain efficient ordinary-to-extraordinary-to-Bernstein-wave conversion despite fluctuating density gradients, launch angle errors, and evolving edge geometry.
status: Electron-Bernstein-wave current drive was demonstrated in W7-AS in 2003; robust reactor-compatible coupling is the unresolved extension.
why: Bernstein waves can access overdense plasma only through a reliable coupling pathway.
key_works: Laqua et al. (2003), *Electron-Bernstein-Wave Current Drive in an Overdense Plasma at the Wendelstein 7-AS Stellarator*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.90.075003.

title: Predictive Bernstein-wave current sign and localization
open: Predict and control the sign and spatial distribution of Bernstein-wave-driven current when harmonics, trapped particles, and relativistic effects compete.
status: Demonstrated current drive establishes feasibility, not a universal profile-control map.
why: A current-drive system must generate the desired current in the desired location.
key_works: Laqua et al. (2003), *Electron-Bernstein-Wave Current Drive in an Overdense Plasma at the Wendelstein 7-AS Stellarator*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.90.075003.

title: Three-ion heating under changing fuel composition
open: Maintain efficient three-ion cyclotron heating while fuel ratios, minority populations, and fast-ion distributions evolve.
status: Three-ion scenarios have substantial experimental and theoretical support; their efficiency depends sensitively on composition and resonant absorbers.
why: A narrow composition window could be difficult to preserve during reactor transients.
key_works: Kazakov et al. (2021), *Physics and applications of three-ion ICRF scenarios for fusion research*, *Physics of Plasmas* 28, 020501.

title: Parasitic absorption in burning-plasma three-ion scenarios
open: Quantify how fusion products, ash, impurities, and beam ions divide RF absorption in a burning plasma, including unwanted energetic-particle drive.
status: The three-ion framework supports multiple absorbing populations; a reactor’s self-consistent mixture introduces additional channels.
why: Power intended for bulk fuel can instead feed weakly confined tails or instabilities.
key_works: Kazakov et al. (2021), *Physics and applications of three-ion ICRF scenarios for fusion research*, *Physics of Plasmas* 28, 020501.

title: Cesium-free negative-ion surfaces at useful throughput
open: Demonstrate a cesium-free surface producing the required negative-ion current density and beam quality while counting source power and electron co-extraction.
status: Diamond-based alternatives have been studied in hydrogen and deuterium plasmas; favorable surface production does not establish a complete high-current source.
why: Eliminating cesium could simplify contamination control and long-pulse operation.
key_works: Cartry et al. (2019), *Alternative solutions to caesium in negative-ion sources: a study of negative-ion surface production on diamond in H₂/D₂ plasmas*, arXiv:1910.05158.

title: Negative-ion surface-state lifetime
open: Determine whether useful electron-affinity and surface-termination states survive prolonged plasma bombardment, contamination, and repeated conditioning.
status: Candidate-surface studies establish production mechanisms; stable operation over industrial duty cycles remains a separate qualification target.
why: A high initial yield is insufficient if the emitting surface rapidly changes.
key_works: Cartry et al. (2019), *Alternative solutions to caesium in negative-ion sources*, arXiv:1910.05158.

title: Composition-dependent pellet-plasmoid drift
open: Predict radial drift of the ablation cloud for mixed-material pellets, including ionization, radiation, magnetic perturbations, and changing electrical conductivity.
status: Three-dimensional MHD modeling published in 2024 advances drift prediction; reliable mixture-dependent assimilation remains a further challenge.
why: Pellet material can drift away from the region where it is needed.
key_works: Kong et al. (2024), *3D MHD modelling of plasmoid drift following massive material injection in a tokamak*, arXiv:2407.01399.

title: Plasmoid current closure and drift saturation
open: Identify the mechanisms limiting ablation-cloud polarization and drift, and validate how parallel current closure changes with geometry and plasma state.
status: Three-dimensional calculations can represent current closure more realistically than simplified drift models; a transferable reduced saturation law remains valuable.
why: Assimilation predictions are sensitive to how far the cloud moves before dispersing.
key_works: Kong et al. (2024), *3D MHD modelling of plasmoid drift following massive material injection in a tokamak*, arXiv:2407.01399; Müller et al. (1999), *High-β Plasmoid Drift during Pellet Injection into Tokamaks*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.83.2199.

title: D–T temperature separation during ignition-scale shocks
open: Quantify deuterium–tritium temperature separation during shock passage and determine its effect on burn inference and subsequent equilibration.
status: Ion thermal decoupling and species separation were demonstrated in shock-driven implosions in 2015; ignition-scale D–T extrapolation remains distinct.
why: A single inferred ion temperature may not determine the correct reaction rate.
key_works: Rinderknecht et al. (2015), *Ion Thermal Decoupling and Species Separation in Shock-Driven Implosions*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.114.025001.

title: Fuel demixing through converging shocks
open: Predict the combined effects of pressure-gradient diffusion, electric fields, and thermal diffusion on local D–T composition during realistic implosion histories.
status: Species-separation experiments establish the phenomenon; quantitative composition evolution in high-gain targets remains a more demanding test.
why: The optimum initial fuel mixture need not remain locally optimal during burn.
key_works: Rinderknecht et al. (2015), *Ion Thermal Decoupling and Species Separation in Shock-Driven Implosions*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.114.025001.

title: Cold contaminant survival in burning hot spots
open: Predict the size distribution and lifetime of contaminant chunks that remain colder than the fuel during burn, including breakup, conduction, and atomic mixing.
status: Experiments published in 2020 observed persistent temperature separation in contaminant–fuel mixtures and challenged instantaneous-equilibration assumptions.
why: Cold inclusions remove energy differently from uniformly mixed hot impurities.
key_works: Haines et al. (2020), *Observation of persistent species temperature separation in inertial confinement fusion mixtures*, DOI: 10.1038/s41467-020-14412-y.

title: Contaminant-mass inference without equilibrium assumptions
open: Infer total contaminant mass while allowing cold, weakly emitting chunks and nonequilibrium temperatures, and validate against independently known contamination.
status: The 2020 study estimated that equilibrium-based methods could underestimate contamination by a factor of two or more in the investigated conditions.
why: Target optimization can be misdirected when the principal loss mechanism is systematically underestimated.
key_works: Haines et al. (2020), *Observation of persistent species temperature separation in inertial confinement fusion mixtures*, DOI: 10.1038/s41467-020-14412-y.

title: Physical versus artificial viscosity in implosion shocks
open: Separate physical plasma viscosity from numerical shock regularization and establish convergence of shock timing, peak temperature, and neutron production with both treated consistently.
status: A 2015 study found significant sensitivity to physical viscosity in spherical implosion calculations.
why: Numerical stabilization should not determine the inferred importance of real dissipation.
key_works: Vold et al. (2015), *Plasma Viscosity with Mass Transport in Spherical ICF Implosion Simulations*, DOI: 10.1063/1.4935906; arXiv:1509.01274.

title: Viscosity-controlled transition to atomic mixing
open: Determine whether evolving plasma viscosity delays or accelerates the transition from interpenetrating material structures to atomically mixed fuel.
status: Viscosity and mass-transport calculations show significant implosion effects, while experiments demonstrate that complete thermal mixing can be slow.
why: The same apparent geometric mixing can produce different radiative and conductive losses.

title: Stopping-power corrections beyond weak coupling
open: Produce experimentally validated charged-particle stopping predictions where weak-coupling expansions, local equilibrium, or homogeneous-background assumptions cease to be sufficiently accurate.
status: Controlled weak-coupling calculations provide an important benchmark; extending their reliability to more difficult implosion states remains open.
why: Small stopping differences affect ignition margins and charged-particle diagnostic interpretation.
key_works: Brown, Preston, and Singleton (2005), *dE/dx to Subleading Order in the Plasma Density*, arXiv:physics/0509168; Singleton (2008), *Charged particle stopping power effects on ignition: Some results from an exact calculation*, arXiv:0712.1023.

title: Knudsen-tail depletion during self-heating
open: Determine whether fusion-relevant high-energy ion tails remain depleted, are replenished, or become anisotropic when nonlocal escape competes with collisions and alpha heating.
status: Approximate ion-kinetic implosion models exist; coupling tail evolution self-consistently to ignition is a stronger problem.
why: Fusion reactivity depends disproportionately on the energetic portion of the distribution.
key_works: Hoffman et al. (2015), *Approximate models for the ion-kinetic regime in inertial-confinement-fusion capsule implosions*, DOI: 10.1063/1.4921130.

title: Nuclear dopants that do not materially perturb implosions
open: Find diagnostic dopant choices and concentrations that provide identifiable signals while bounding their effects on opacity, ablation, mixing, and yield.
status: The first bromine-doped cryogenic experiment reported a yield 2.6 times lower than its undoped comparison; signal feasibility does not imply diagnostic nonintrusiveness.
why: A diagnostic should not substantially alter the phenomenon it is intended to measure.
key_works: Hayes et al. (2023), *First bromine doped cryogenic implosion at the National Ignition Facility*, DOI: 10.1063/5.0142596; arXiv:2307.03730.

title: Nuclear-diagnostic reaction and collection uncertainties
open: Separate uncertainty in reaction cross-sections, energetic-ion distributions, product transport, and sample collection when inferring implosion properties from activation products.
status: Bromine-dopant experiments demonstrate measurable nuclear signatures, but a robust inverse model must account for several coupled stages.
why: A precise isotope count does not automatically produce a precise plasma measurement.
key_works: Hayes et al. (2023), *First bromine doped cryogenic implosion at the National Ignition Facility*, arXiv:2307.03730.

title: Predictive non-LTE hohlraum emission
open: Construct atomic-kinetics models that predict ignition-scale hohlraum spectra and drive without experiment-specific correction multipliers.
status: Improved non-LTE modeling was published in 2025; matching the full spectrum and target drive remains the relevant test.
why: An incorrect radiation spectrum can change both ablation and preheat.
key_works: Farmer et al. (2025), *Toward an improved nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium model for more predictive simulations of ignition scale hohlraums*, DOI: 10.1063/5.0267536.

title: Unmodified prediction of NIF bang time
open: Predict bang time across a held-out family of indirect-drive experiments without retuning radiation-drive multipliers for each design.
status: The Build-A-Hohlraum campaign investigates longstanding simulation discrepancies and identifies spectral evidence pointing toward atomic-model shortcomings.
why: Timing errors obscure whether a design problem comes from the capsule or its drive.
key_works: Swadling et al. (2025), *Resolving discrepancies in bang-time predictions for indirect-drive ICF experiments on the NIF: Insights from the Build-A-Hohlraum campaign*, arXiv:2501.10350.

title: Spectral corrections transferable across hohlraum designs
open: Determine whether improvements resolving one hohlraum’s hard-x-ray discrepancy remain valid across wall materials, gas fills, geometry, and laser pulse histories.
status: Build-A-Hohlraum experiments constrain candidate explanations; a correction fitted to one campaign is not yet a universally predictive atomic model.
why: A design tool must transfer beyond the shots used to calibrate it.
key_works: Swadling et al. (2025), *Resolving discrepancies in bang-time predictions for indirect-drive ICF experiments on the NIF*, arXiv:2501.10350.

title: Multispecies interpenetration in ignition-scale hohlraums
open: Predict wall-plasma and fill-gas interpenetration using validated multispecies transport rather than numerical mixing or a single-fluid approximation.
status: Direct experimental evidence of multispecies hydrodynamics in ignition-scale hohlraums was published in 2025.
why: Species separation changes laser propagation, emission, and the radiation environment of the capsule.
key_works: Higginson et al. (2025), *Direct Evidence of Multispecies Hydrodynamics in Ignition-Scale Hohlraums*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.134.165101.

title: Magnetized alpha deposition in ignition-class targets
open: Experimentally validate the predicted redistribution of alpha heating when externally imposed magnetic fields are compressed in an ignition-class implosion.
status: Integrated 2026 simulations predict significant benefits from magnetization; these are modeled enhancements, not measured gain records.
why: Magnetic insulation is useful only if its full effect on alpha heating and burn is favorable.
key_works: Djordjević et al. (2026), *Integrated Radiation-Magneto-Hydrodynamic Simulations of Magnetized Burning Plasmas. I. Magnetizing Ignition-Class Designs*, arXiv:2601.02588.

title: Magnetization–symmetry tradeoff
open: Optimize applied-field strength and target geometry while accounting for anisotropic heat flow, changed hohlraum coupling, and implosion asymmetry.
status: The 2026 integrated simulations show that magnetization and symmetrization interact; simply adding a stronger field is not a complete optimization rule.
why: Improved insulation can be offset by less spherical compression.
key_works: Djordjević et al. (2026), *Integrated Radiation-Magneto-Hydrodynamic Simulations of Magnetized Burning Plasmas. I*, arXiv:2601.02588.

title: Imprint suppression without unacceptable preheat
open: Determine the coating composition and thickness window that suppresses laser imprint while bounding additional radiation, preheat, and ablator contamination.
status: Thin high-Z coatings demonstrated imprint suppression in 2015; the complete target-performance tradeoff remains design-dependent.
why: Suppressing initial perturbations is useful only if the coating does not create a larger loss.
key_works: Karasik et al. (2015), *Suppression of Laser Nonuniformity Imprinting Using a Thin High-Z Coating*, DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.114.085001.

title: Foam-mediated imprint control at ignition scale
open: Validate how porous-layer structure and early pulse shaping smooth laser imprint when foam microstructure, ionization, and hydrodynamic expansion are resolved.
status: Foam-plastic shaping-pulse studies date to 2002; scalable target benefits require more than reproducing a reduced imprint measurement.
why: A manufacturable smoothing layer could reduce driver-uniformity requirements.
key_works: Metzler et al. (2002), *Laser imprint reduction with a short shaping laser pulse incident upon a foam-plastic target*, *Physics of Plasmas* 9, 5050.

title: Graded inner shells robust to fabrication uncertainty
open: Optimize double-shell material gradients against measured uncertainty in thickness, composition, surface finish, and assembly—not only nominal simulated yield.
status: Multifidelity optimization has identified promising graded-shell designs; robust experimental realization remains a further step.
why: A narrow numerical optimum may have poor manufacturing yield.
key_works: Vazirani et al. (2023), *Coupling multi-fidelity xRAGE with machine learning for graded inner shell design optimization in double shell capsules*, *Physics of Plasmas* 30, 062704.

title: Perturbation transmission through successive shell collisions
open: Predict how perturbations are amplified, filtered, or transferred through every collision in a multiple-shell target, including the final fuel-containing shell.
status: OMEGA experiments validated an important outer-shell collision in the Revolver concept in 2019; this is not validation of the complete multi-collision ignition sequence.
why: Favorable energy transfer can coexist with damaging instability transfer.
key_works: Scheiner et al. (2019), *First experiments on Revolver shell collisions at the OMEGA Laser*, DOI: 10.1063/1.5099975; arXiv:1904.07086.

title: Chirping criteria far from marginal stability
open: Extend chirping-versus-steady-frequency criteria to strongly driven modes with evolving backgrounds and significant redistribution of energetic particles.
status: Existing criteria incorporate collisions and turbulence and have experimental comparisons; near-threshold reasoning does not automatically cover strongly nonlinear bursts.
why: Different nonlinear mode behavior produces very different particle-loss risks.
key_works: Duarte et al. (2017), *Prediction of Nonlinear Evolution Character of Energetic-Particle-Driven Instabilities*, PPPL-5366.

title: Hole–clump survival in turbulent phase space
open: Predict the lifetime and trajectory of phase-space holes and clumps when collisions, background turbulence, multiple resonances, and changing mode structure act simultaneously.
status: Chirping theory identifies the relevant competition; a transferable lifetime model for realistic multimode plasmas remains unresolved.
why: Long-lived coherent structures can transport energetic particles far beyond a local resonance.
key_works: Duarte et al. (2017), *Prediction of Nonlinear Evolution Character of Energetic-Particle-Driven Instabilities*, PPPL-5366.

title: Self-consistent resonance broadening
open: Determine resonance widths from collisions, mode evolution, and nonlinear trapping without selecting an empirical broadening prescription independently of the transport calculation.
status: Discrete-resonance quasilinear work supplies collisionally broadened response functions; full nonlinear self-consistency remains more demanding.
why: Resonance width controls whether neighboring modes remain separate or produce global transport.
key_works: Duarte et al. (2019), *Collisional resonance function in discrete-resonance quasilinear plasma systems*, *Physics of Plasmas* 26, 120701.

title: Energetic-particle avalanches with replenishment
open: Determine how continuous particle sources, slowing down, and sinks change avalanche recurrence and long-time transport.
status: A 2026 study analyzes nondiffusive avalanche transport in a reduced multimode model; including realistic replenishment is a distinct extension.
why: A reactor continuously creates alpha particles rather than evolving a single isolated initial population.
key_works: Carlevaro et al. (2026), *Analysis of non-diffusive avalanche transport of energetic particles*, DOI: 10.1016/j.physd.2026.135286; arXiv:2409.12644.

title: Three-dimensional validity of reduced avalanche models
open: Establish when avalanche behavior inferred from reduced wave–particle models survives full orbit geometry, finite orbit width, and self-consistent mode evolution.
status: Reduced models reveal transport missed by simple diffusion; their quantitative mapping to realistic toroidal plasmas remains the key validation question.
why: A convincing reduced-model avalanche is not yet a reliable reactor loss prediction.
key_works: Carlevaro et al. (2026), *Analysis of non-diffusive avalanche transport of energetic particles*, arXiv:2409.12644.

title: Causal confinement benefit of energetic-ion modes
open: Separate confinement improvement caused by energetic-ion-mode-generated flows from improvement caused by the heating, profiles, or operating conditions that also produce the modes.
status: JET D–T results published in 2024 report stable plasmas with improved confinement in the presence of energetic-ion instabilities.
why: Beneficial correlations are not sufficient grounds for deliberately exciting an instability.
key_works: Garcia et al. (2024), *Stable Deuterium-Tritium plasmas with improved confinement in the presence of energetic-ion instabilities*, DOI: 10.1038/s41467-024-52182-z.

title: Safe beneficial-instability operating windows
open: Determine when energetic-particle modes regulate turbulence beneficially and when the same mode family produces unacceptable particle loss or wall loading.
status: Improved-confinement observations establish that energetic-particle activity is not uniformly harmful; they do not establish a broadly safe control strategy.
why: Exploiting an instability requires knowing where its benefit changes sign.
key_works: Garcia et al. (2024), *Stable Deuterium-Tritium plasmas with improved confinement in the presence of energetic-ion instabilities*, DOI: 10.1038/s41467-024-52182-z.

title: Time-resolved fast-ion distribution reconstruction
open: Reconstruct evolving fast-ion distributions during bursts with enough temporal and phase-space resolution to distinguish transport mechanisms, while reporting nonuniqueness.
status: A 2025 JET study reconstructed a fast-deuterium distribution in a D–T discharge; burst-resolved multidimensional reconstruction is a stronger target.
why: Mode amplitude alone does not reveal which particles moved or were lost.
key_works: Järleblad et al. (2025), *Reconstruction of the fast-ion deuterium distribution in a tritium-rich plasma in the JET DTE2 campaign*, DOI: 10.1088/1741-4326/ad9b39.

title: Externally driven whistler mitigation of runaways
open: Demonstrate that externally supplied whistler waves reduce harmful runaway-electron energy or wall loading after including coupling efficiency and the evolving electron distribution.
status: Runaway-driven whistlers have been observed; spontaneous wave emission does not establish an effective external mitigation actuator.
why: Wave-mediated scattering could complement material injection and magnetic mitigation.
key_works: Spong et al. (2018), *First Direct Observation of Runaway-Electron-Driven Whistler Waves in Tokamaks*; Casolari et al. (2022), *Whistler wave destabilization by a runaway electron beam in COMPASS*.

title: Whistler wave-number and resonance identification
open: Measure the wave-vector distribution and damping of runaway-driven whistlers sufficiently well to determine which electron energies and pitch angles they actually scatter.
status: Detailed DIII-D characterization published in 2025 improves frequency and temporal constraints; frequency measurements alone do not uniquely identify resonance.
why: An observed wave may couple weakly to the electrons responsible for damage.
key_works: Choudhury et al. (2025), *Detailed characterization of runaway electron driven whistler waves in low-density DIII-D discharges*, DOI: 10.1063/5.0277589.

title: Experimental validation of weak wave-driven depolarization
open: Test predicted nuclear-spin survival in controlled plasma-wave environments and establish bounds on depolarization over fuel-confinement times.
status: September 2025 first-principles calculations predict weak depolarization for important alpha-driven Alfvénic modes in SPARC- and ITER-scale conditions.
why: Favorable calculations strengthen the polarized-fuel case but require experimental confirmation.
key_works: Cook et al. (2025), *Persistence of Deuterium and Tritium Nuclear Spin-Polarization in Presence of High-Frequency Plasma Waves*, arXiv:2509.25506.

title: Depolarization from combined wave spectra
open: Determine whether many individually weak wave-driven depolarization channels combine coherently, diffusively, or nonlinearly into a significant loss.
status: The 2025 study finds reassuring behavior for examined instabilities; an evolving broadband spectrum and rare resonant excursions require further assessment.
why: Small single-mode effects do not automatically bound cumulative polarization loss.
key_works: Cook et al. (2025), *Persistence of Deuterium and Tritium Nuclear Spin-Polarization in Presence of High-Frequency Plasma Waves*, arXiv:2509.25506.

title: Blanket-flow wall-mode transitions
open: Predict transitions between laminar, wall-localized, and chaotic flow structures in magnetized blanket channels with strong heating.
status: Recent magnetoconvection studies characterize wall modes and transitions in controlled geometries; reactor-channel transfer remains unresolved.
why: Strong magnetic damping does not guarantee a simple or steady velocity field.
key_works: McCormack et al. (2023), *Wall mode dynamics and transition to chaos in magnetoconvection with a vertical magnetic field*, DOI: 10.1017/jfm.2023.863.

title: Buoyancy–Lorentz crossover in blanket heat transfer
open: Establish a heat-transfer closure spanning buoyancy-dominated and magnetically dominated regimes with realistic wall conduction and channel orientation.
status: A 2024 unifying magnetoconvection model addresses the crossover; blanket geometry and material coupling require further validation.
why: Incorrect crossover behavior can conceal hot spots or overstate heat-removal capacity.
key_works: Teimurazov et al. (2024), *Unifying heat transport model for the transition between buoyancy-dominated and Lorentz-force-dominated regimes in quasistatic magnetoconvection*, DOI: 10.1017/jfm.2024.33.

title: Field-orientation sensitivity of liquid-metal convection
open: Quantify how changes in magnetic-field direction relative to gravity and heated walls alter flow morphology and peak temperatures.
status: Direct studies of horizontal-field liquid-metal convection published in 2024 demonstrate that orientation is not a minor correction.
why: A blanket experiences three-dimensional fields and multiple channel orientations.
key_works: Chen, Yang, and Ni (2024), *Effects of horizontal magnetic fields on flow morphologies and global transports in liquid metal thermal convection*, DOI: 10.1017/jfm.2024.1002.

title: Electrical coupling between neighboring blanket channels
open: Predict current closure through shared walls and manifolds when multiple liquid-metal channels have different temperatures, velocities, or insulation damage.
status: Liquid-metal blanket research identifies three-dimensional MHD and electrical-wall effects; independently modeled channels can miss collective behavior.
why: A fault or flow change in one channel can alter pressure drop and cooling elsewhere.
key_works: Smolentsev, Moreau, Bühler, and Mistrangelo (2010), *MHD thermofluid issues of liquid-metal blankets: Phenomena and advances*, *Fusion Engineering and Design* 85, 1196–1205.

title: Permeator boundary-layer versus membrane limitation
open: Identify which resistance limits tritium extraction under each operating condition and validate transitions between liquid-side transport, interface kinetics, and membrane diffusion.
status: Vacuum-permeator parameter studies exist; treating all cases as membrane-limited can misidentify the useful engineering intervention.
why: Increasing membrane area or permeability may provide little benefit when another stage dominates.
key_works: Fuerst et al. (2023), *Parametric Study of the Vacuum Permeator for the Tritium …* (full title verify), OSTI:1987842.

title: Permeator surface poisoning and recovery
open: Determine how oxides, corrosion products, and trace contaminants change isotope-transfer kinetics, and demonstrate recoverable performance after representative contamination.
status: Permeator studies establish design sensitivities; long-duration surface chemistry remains separate from clean-system transport performance.
why: A high initial extraction rate does not establish dependable fuel recovery.
key_works: Fuerst et al. (2023), vacuum-permeator parametric study, OSTI:1987842; Humrickhouse et al. (2017), *Tritium aspects of the fusion nuclear science facility*.

title: Vacuum-sieve-tray droplet population control
open: Predict extraction from the complete droplet-size and residence-time distribution, including coalescence, breakup, entrainment, and changing surface condition.
status: Vacuum-sieve-tray extraction is an actively developed liquid-metal fuel-cycle approach; a nominal droplet size does not close the mass-transfer problem.
why: Effective interfacial area determines both extraction rate and equipment size.
key_works: Kyoto Fusioneering (2025), *The VST Explained: Unlocking Tritium Extraction*.

title: Hot-atom tritium chemistry in lead–lithium
open: Determine how newly produced energetic tritium partitions among chemical states before thermal equilibrium, and whether this changes recoverability or retention.
