status: Lithium-tritide formation through hot-atom reactions in Pb–16Li was studied in 2013; coupling that chemistry to operating extraction systems remains open.
why: Breeding calculations count nuclei, while extraction systems respond to chemical species.
key_works: Okuno et al. (2013), *Formation of lithium-tritide by hot atom reactions of tritium produced in Pb-16Li*, *Fusion Engineering and Design* 88, 2328–2331.

title: Intrinsic FLiBe permeability separated from interface artifacts
open: Measure bulk hydrogen-isotope transport independently of incomplete wetting, trapped gas, membrane coverage, and charging geometry.
status: HYPERION results published in 2026 found that interface effects could change apparent permeability by as much as 77% in investigated conditions.
why: A measured apparatus property should not be entered into reactor models as a bulk material constant.
key_works: Saraswat et al. (2026), *Permeation behaviour of hydrogen isotopes in molten FLiBe (2LiF–BeF₂): Identifying sources of uncertainty and associated measurement challenges*, DOI: 10.1016/j.ijhydene.2026.156016; arXiv:2603.28991.

title: Hydrogen/deuterium-to-tritium transport extrapolation
open: Establish when isotope scaling remains valid for molten-salt transport once interface kinetics, chemical speciation, and trapping are included.
status: HYPERION demonstrates that interfaces can suppress expected isotopic behavior; simple mass scaling is therefore not automatically justified.
why: Tritium measurements are difficult, but surrogate measurements must retain predictive value.
key_works: Saraswat et al. (2026), *Permeation behaviour of hydrogen isotopes in molten FLiBe*, arXiv:2603.28991.

title: Light-element speciation in operating molten salts
open: Identify and quantify hydrogen-bearing species in chemically complex fluoride salts under controlled redox state, impurities, and irradiation-relevant conditions.
status: Dedicated molten-salt speciation programs exist; bulk concentration alone does not determine transport or corrosion behavior.
why: Extraction, permeation, and safety models depend on chemical form.
key_works: University of California, Berkeley, SALT program, *Probing Speciation of Light Elements in Molten Salts*.

title: Irradiation-driven salt chemistry versus equilibrium redox
open: Determine whether radiolysis creates persistent reactive species or local chemical conditions that are missed by equilibrium redox models.
status: Radiolysis modeling for FLiBe is an active 2026 research topic; reactor-relevant experimental constraints remain limited.
why: Nominally controlled bulk redox may not prevent localized corrosive chemistry.
key_works: Peterkin (2026), *Modeling Radiolysis Effects in FLiBe Molten Fluoride Salt*, DOE NNSA fellowship research presentation.

title: Tritium-accounting closure during integral breeding tests
open: Close the balance among produced, extracted, dissolved, trapped, permeated, and sampled tritium in an irradiated molten-salt experiment with an auditable uncertainty budget.
status: LIBRA was designed specifically to investigate robust accountancy in FLiBe exposed to a D–T neutron spectrum.
why: Apparent breeding or extraction success can hide unmeasured retention or leakage.
key_works: Ferry et al. (2022), *The LIBRA Experiment: Investigating Robust Tritium Accountancy in Molten FLiBe Exposed to a D–T Fusion Neutron Spectrum*, MIT repository handle:1721.1/147635.

title: Coupled coarsening of two-phase ceramic breeders
open: Predict how lithium orthosilicate/metatitanate phase fractions, grain sizes, porosity, and interfaces evolve together under prolonged service.
status: Long-term thermal-stability work was published in 2018; irradiation and lithium-consumption effects add further evolution mechanisms.
why: The microstructure controlling release and strength is not static.
key_works: Heuser et al. (2018), *Long-term thermal stability of two-phased lithium orthosilicate/metatitanate ceramics*, DOI: 10.1016/j.jnucmat.2018.05.010.

title: Breeder performance under lithium depletion
open: Determine how spatially nonuniform lithium consumption changes ceramic chemistry, mechanical behavior, tritium release, and local breeding over time.
status: Thermal-stability studies constrain part of the problem; depletion-driven composition evolution is an additional service-history effect.
why: Initial breeder qualification may not represent its end-of-life state.
key_works: Heuser et al. (2018), *Long-term thermal stability of two-phased lithium orthosilicate/metatitanate ceramics*, DOI: 10.1016/j.jnucmat.2018.05.010; Abdou et al. (2015), *Blanket/first wall challenges and required R&D on the pathway to DEMO*.

title: Retention versus release under simultaneous in-core production
open: Distinguish transport parameters measured by post-irradiation release from those governing tritium generated continuously inside the breeder.
status: In-core generation, release, and retention studies exist; ex situ desorption does not necessarily reproduce the steady production–trapping balance.
why: A material that releases stored tritium well after irradiation may still accumulate it during operation.
key_works: Dolan et al. (2020), *Tritium generation, release, and retention from in-core …* (full title verify), OSTI:1850462.

title: Continuous selective-adsorption isotope separation
open: Convert promising batch adsorption selectivity into a continuous or cyclic process with quantified purity, recovery, throughput, inventory, and energy consumption.
status: A 2025 Ag-exchanged-zeolite study enriched tritium to 70% from an initially equimolar three-isotope mixture; industrial separation is a further step.
why: High equilibrium selectivity alone does not establish a useful fuel-cycle unit.
key_works: Becker et al. (2025), *Tritium Separation from Gaseous 1,2,3H Isotopologue Mixtures by Selective Adsorption on Ag-Exchanged Zeolite Type Y*, arXiv:2510.03333.

title: Radiation and impurity durability of isotope sorbents
open: Measure whether isotope-selective sorbents retain capacity and selectivity after tritium exposure, radiolysis, moisture, impurities, and repeated regeneration.
status: The 2025 zeolite result establishes separation performance in investigated experiments, not long-life fuel-processing qualification.
why: Sorbent replacement and contamination could negate an otherwise attractive separation method.
key_works: Becker et al. (2025), *Tritium Separation from Gaseous 1,2,3H Isotopologue Mixtures by Selective Adsorption on Ag-Exchanged Zeolite Type Y*, arXiv:2510.03333.

title: Low-temperature decomposition of tritiated ammonia
open: Demonstrate sufficiently complete ammonia decomposition at temperatures compatible with downstream isotope-separation equipment and acceptable tritium inventory.
status: Dedicated 2024 research addresses tritiated ammonia as a fusion by-product; activity, selectivity, and downstream compatibility must be optimized together.
why: Ammonia can bind useful fuel and interfere with purification systems.
key_works: Naglic (2024), *Applications of Catalytic Ammonia Chemistry: From Low-Pressure Ammonia Synthesis to the Decomposition of Tritiated Ammonia as a By-Product of Magnetically Confined Nuclear Fusion*, University of South Carolina dissertation, ETD:7912.

title: Catalyst lifetime in tritiated impurity streams
open: Qualify ammonia-decomposition catalysts against hydrogen isotopes, water, hydrocarbons, radiolysis products, and repeated startup or regeneration.
status: Catalyst investigations establish candidate approaches; real-stream lifetime and recoverability remain separate from clean-feed conversion.
why: Slow catalyst degradation can silently increase bound-tritium inventory.
key_works: Naglic (2024), *Applications of Catalytic Ammonia Chemistry*, ETD:7912; Angelette et al. (2021), *Evaluation of catalysts for decomposition of ammonia in …* (full title verify).

title: Predictive ammonia formation under radiolysis
open: Predict formation and destruction of tritiated ammonia in realistic nitrogen–hydrogen-isotope mixtures, including surfaces and continuous beta irradiation.
status: Tritiated-ammonia formation was studied by the 1990s; modern exhaust compositions and operating histories require renewed quantitative closure.
why: A decomposition unit cannot be sized reliably without knowing the upstream formation rate.
key_works: Heung (1995), *Tritiated ammonia formation*, *Fusion Technology* 28, 1188–1193.

title: Distinguishing self-radiolysis from catalytic conversion
open: Separate spontaneous isotope-dependent radiolysis, wall-catalyzed reactions, and intentional catalyst performance in tritium-bearing molecular experiments.
status: Self-radiolysis has long been recognized in tritiated compounds; it can confound long-duration process measurements.
why: Apparent catalyst performance may partly reflect time-dependent chemistry elsewhere in the apparatus.
key_works: Glugla et al. (1988), *On the Synthesis, Selfradiolysis, and Catalytic …* (full title verify), DOI: 10.13182/FST88-A25213.

title: Calibrated spectroscopy of tritiated ammonia isotopologues
open: Establish validated reference spectra and response factors for tritiated ammonia species, including mixed isotopologues and interfering gases.
status: A 2025 hydrogen/ammonia detection study identifies further tritiated-species calibration as a needed extension.
why: Uncalibrated signals cannot close impurity or tritium balances.
key_works: Kelly et al. (2025), *Real-Time Detection of Hydrogen and Ammonia Isotopologues for Impurity Removal and Recovery of Tritium*, DOI: 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c01241.

title: Real-time separation of overlapping isotope signals
open: Infer changing hydrogen and ammonia isotopologue concentrations despite overlapping spectral features, pressure shifts, temperature changes, and detector drift.
status: Real-time spectroscopic detection is demonstrated; robust mixed-stream inversion with quantified uncertainty remains a stronger operating requirement.
why: Fuel-cycle control needs reliable composition estimates while the stream changes.
key_works: Kelly et al. (2025), *Real-Time Detection of Hydrogen and Ammonia Isotopologues for Impurity Removal and Recovery of Tritium*, DOI: 10.1021/acs.analchem.5c01241.

title: Ortho–para conversion in tritium process equipment
open: Measure conversion kinetics and heat release for hydrogen-isotope spin isomers on relevant surfaces and incorporate them into cryogenic process models.
status: Recent tritium infrared experiments explicitly address molecular-state and phase-property gaps; spin composition can affect both measurements and thermal behavior.
why: Unmodeled conversion can distort cryogenic heat balances and inferred composition.
key_works: Marsteller et al. (2025 preprint), *First results of the Tritium Absorption InfraRed Spectroscopy (T₂ApIR) experiment*, arXiv:2512.19757.

title: Mixed-isotopologue phase-transition properties
open: Measure phase boundaries, latent heat, density, and kinetic hysteresis for relevant mixtures of all six hydrogen isotopologues, rather than extrapolating only from pure species.
status: T₂ApIR is designed to investigate gaseous, liquid, solid, and phase-transition behavior; experimentally verified tritium properties remain sparse.
why: Pellet production and cryogenic separation both depend on mixture behavior.
key_works: Marsteller et al. (2025), *First results of the Tritium Absorption InfraRed Spectroscopy (T₂ApIR) experiment*, arXiv:2512.19757.

title: Separation factor versus throughput in lithium-isotope methods
open: Establish whether mercury-free lithium-isotope separation approaches retain useful selectivity at practical throughput, durability, and environmental burden.
status: A 2025 review documents active alternatives; laboratory selectivity is not equivalent to an economical supply process.
why: Blanket deployment needs a credible supply chain without shifting unacceptable environmental costs elsewhere.
key_works: He et al. (2025), *Progress and Perspectives of Lithium Isotope Separation*, DOI: 10.1002/cphc.202400999.

title: Lifetime of lithium-isotope selective media
open: Determine how selective membranes, resins, and complexing media age under repeated processing, and whether degradation changes isotope selectivity before bulk performance visibly fails.
status: Multiple alternative separation mechanisms are under investigation; service-life evidence is less mature than proof-of-selectivity experiments.
why: Consumable lifetime can dominate the cost and environmental footprint of a separation route.
key_works: Badea et al. (2023), *New Trends in Separation Techniques of Lithium Isotopes*; He et al. (2025), DOI: 10.1002/cphc.202400999.

title: Cryogenic separation with spin-state nonequilibrium
open: Predict isotope-column behavior when ortho–para populations are not in local equilibrium and conversion occurs unevenly on packing or catalyst surfaces.
status: Cryogenic isotope separation is established, and dedicated ortho–para studies exist; equilibrium-only descriptions do not settle this coupled transient problem.
why: Spin-state evolution can change both separation behavior and refrigeration demand.
key_works: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, *Separation of ortho para hydrogen by cryogenic distillation*; Marsteller et al. (2025), arXiv:2512.19757.

title: Trace impurity accumulation over repeated fuel cycles
open: Predict which slowly removed impurities accumulate in a closed tritium loop and establish detection and removal thresholds before they degrade catalysts, membranes, or plasma performance.
status: Tritium technology assessments identify interacting processing stages; individually acceptable impurity passage can become unacceptable after repeated recycling.
why: A closed loop amplifies small systematic separation imperfections.
key_works: Glugla et al. (2023 report), *Tritium Technology for Fusion Devices—Status and R&D Needs*, UKAEA-CCFE-PR(23)99.

title: Versioned atomic-rate provenance in plasma codes
open: Make every effective atomic or molecular rate traceable to underlying cross-sections, state-population assumptions, isotope transformations, fit ranges, and code versions.
status: The 2023 molecular-charge-exchange investigation shows that seemingly minor rate-processing choices can change detachment conclusions.
why: Reproducing a simulation requires reproducing its atomic assumptions, not only its source-code commit.
key_works: Verhaegh et al. (2023), *Investigating the impact of the molecular charge-exchange rate on detached SOLPS-ITER simulations*, DOI: 10.1088/1741-4326/acd394.

title: Blind detached-plasma chemistry benchmark
open: Establish held-out discharges in which competing reaction datasets predict target fluxes, molecular emission, pressure, and power balance before seeing the measurements.
status: Current studies often diagnose discrepancies using the same experiments that motivate rate changes; blind multi-observable tests would provide stronger discrimination.
why: Fitting one emission line can worsen the underlying particle or energy balance.
key_works: Verhaegh et al. (2023), arXiv:2311.08580; Osborne et al. (2024–2025), arXiv:2410.14403.

title: Opacity-aware divertor diagnostic benchmark
open: Compare spectroscopic inference methods on shared cases spanning optically thin and thick conditions, with independent constraints on temperature, density, and recombination.
status: A 2025 JET study incorporates Lyman opacity into two-dimensional Balmer-camera analysis; cross-method validation remains valuable.
why: Diagnostic algorithms can agree with each other while sharing the same opacity error.
key_works: Karhunen et al. (2025), *Addressing the impact of Lyman opacity in inference of divertor plasma conditions with 2D spectroscopic camera analysis of Balmer emission during detachment in JET L-mode plasmas*, DOI: 10.1016/j.nme.2025.101880.

title: Interlaboratory molten-salt permeability round robin
open: Reconcile measurements using common salt characterization, interface preparation, geometry reporting, and blinded samples, with separate uncertainty budgets for bulk and interface effects.
status: HYPERION provides a plausible explanation for substantial historical scatter, making an interlaboratory test especially timely.
why: A shared material-property value is unreliable when laboratories measure different hidden interfaces.
key_works: Saraswat et al. (2026), *Permeation behaviour of hydrogen isotopes in molten FLiBe*, arXiv:2603.28991.

title: Uncertainty-certified fast-ion inversion challenge
open: Test reconstruction methods on synthetic and experimental cases with concealed distributions, deliberately weakly constrained populations, and calibrated uncertainty requirements.
status: JET D–T reconstruction demonstrates the capability’s promise; a realistic benchmark should test whether algorithms correctly admit nonuniqueness.
why: Overconfident reconstruction can invent or erase the particles responsible for instability.
key_works: Järleblad et al. (2025), *Reconstruction of the fast-ion deuterium distribution in a tritium-rich plasma in the JET DTE2 campaign*, DOI: 10.1088/1741-4326/ad9b39.

title: Releaseable coil-optimization optimality certificates
open: Publish reproducible cases with optimization objectives, constraints, relaxation gaps, and realizable coil reconstructions so that global-optimality claims can be independently checked.
status: QUADCOIL explicitly distinguishes exact global solutions from approximate ones; standardized certificates would make that distinction auditable.
why: Comparing only final objective values can conceal different feasible sets or unverified relaxations.
key_works: Fu et al. (2024–2025), *Global Stellarator Coil Optimization with Quadratic Constraints and Objectives*, arXiv:2408.08267.

title: Shared state-resolved molecular-collision measurements
open: Establish sustained experimental access for difficult isotope- and state-resolved molecular reactions, prioritized by demonstrated sensitivity of fusion predictions.
status: IAEA atomic-data activities and divertor studies identify continuing needs for tungsten and hydrogen molecular/ionic data; maintaining measurements and evaluated datasets is an infrastructure problem.
why: Code development cannot compensate for missing or weakly constrained reaction physics.
key_works: IAEA, *Tungsten and Hydrogen Ions in Edge Plasmas* technical-meeting program; Verhaegh et al. (2023), DOI: 10.1088/1741-4326/acd394.

title: Shared tritium-compatible qualification of separation media
open: Provide controlled, independently interpretable testing of candidate membranes, sorbents, catalysts, and sensors using representative tritium-bearing mixtures and aging histories.
status: Promising separation demonstrations coexist with fuel-cycle technology gaps; access to appropriately controlled tritium experiments is an enabling infrastructure requirement.
why: Hydrogen-only tests cannot establish every isotope, radiolysis, or inventory effect.
key_works: Glugla et al. (2023 report), *Tritium Technology for Fusion Devices—Status and R&D Needs*; Becker et al. (2025), arXiv:2510.03333.

title: Tenfold faster validated collision calculations
open: Achieve a proposed 10× reduction in the cost of full nonlinear collision calculations while preserving specified conservation, positivity, entropy, and transport-error tolerances on held-out plasma cases.
status: Exact operators and structure-preserving discretizations provide a baseline; speedup alone is not success if it changes nonlinear transport.
why: Collision accuracy is often traded away because it is expensive.
key_works: Jorge et al. (2019), *Nonlinear Gyrokinetic Coulomb Collision Operator*, arXiv:1906.03252; Hirvijoki et al. (2018), arXiv:1804.08546.

title: Industrially repeatable isotope-selective adsorption
open: Demonstrate a proposed benchmark of 10,000 separation/regeneration cycles with less than 10% degradation in both working capacity and isotope selectivity, while reporting full energy and inventory costs.
status: Recent selective-adsorption results establish promising laboratory separation; this proposed endurance benchmark is not an achieved record or an established universal requirement.
why: Repeatability would distinguish a useful process material from a one-time laboratory result.
key_works: Becker et al. (2025), *Tritium Separation from Gaseous 1,2,3H Isotopologue Mixtures by Selective Adsorption on Ag-Exchanged Zeolite Type Y*, arXiv:2510.03333.
